MCP cleanups: sessions_roster is now agents_lookup with view roster and pack_machines_list is computers_list with detail specs (the old names still answer), task_manager_delete is no longer an MCP tool (an agent asks with task_manager_state_request action delete), huddle_focus is switched off by default, and whoami, alerts_list, automation_get, automation_run_get and session_notes_get describe what they return
a conversation deep search reads from the backup shows its session name, project and folder instead of untitled conversation
a session over its usage limit paints a static red skull in the status light, with the limit and its reset time as its words, on every surface that draws the light

a session that hit its Claude usage limit (or a Codex usage_limit_exceeded turn) now carries a usage_limit field on the session listing, read from what the harness wrote, with its kind and reset time, and a background agent that died on the limit no longer leaves the row stuck at working_subagent
a session that never received a first message can now be killed and restarted: it comes back as a new conversation instead of the restart staying disabled with no transcript
a sleeping session that something scheduled will wake keeps its alarm clock icon in the left bar, with the same colors and tooltip as when it is awake

an installed skill in warez now opens its own page: a title bar with a favorite star and a red skull to remove it, a brief card, a details card with fired counts and checks, the formatted SKILL.md with view md, edit, save version and roll back, and an inspector with the state switches per harness and where the skill lives

an untagged scheduled task in a project whose only sessions are asleep now shows the session it will wake in the schedules list, and the sleeping row keeps its alarm clock for that same session (the asleep lead first, else the newest)
beast mode is part of the app again, no longer a plugin: its grid moved to Settings, Advanced, your stored boxes carried over once, and the switch stays in the account menu; behavior is unchanged

catalog (warez) skills now sync by reference: alpha names the item and version, and every other computer installs that same item and version from its own signed catalog, with its own review and revocation checks, instead of receiving bytes
closed sessions no longer appear in the agents sidebar in any band, group, fold or pin; they stay on the sessions and projects pages, and a pinned closed session keeps its pin

copy diagnostics now includes the tmux server pid and session names on both sockets, the last 2 MiB of each known log (redacted, failing closed), and the menu bar launch agent state; a dev run writes its server log where the breadcrumb can point at it
core no longer imports the review board plugin: ui_show asks a board pages port the plugin registers, and answers not found while the plugin is off (#1874)

creating a project at the projects base folder, or at a folder that holds other live projects, is refused with a clear message instead of swallowing them; an exited session with no transcript on disk now reads closed instead of asleep
creating a project or session on a paired computer no longer fails with launch profile does not exist: the paired computer launches its own default profile of the chosen agent family
crosstalk cards are part of the app, no longer a plugin: the switches moved to Settings, Terminal, off for a new install, and an install that had the plugin on keeps its cards and choices
crosstalk messages carry an optional task item id so a task is traceable across sessions: a reply inherits it, and the task manager item shows a crosstalk trail (who to whom, when, first line)

deep search is built into the app instead of being a plugin: it is always on, its card left the plugins page, the drawer's context mode is a core mode, and what it reads (people only, people plus headless sessions, everything) is now a setting in settings under the pipeline tab; routes moved to /api/v1/deepsearch and a stored choice carries over

deep search keeps a conversation findable after Claude Code deletes its file, reading it straight from the conversation backups with no extra copy, Codex and sub-agent files included; results say from backup, and a conversation held by an export bundle says exported, in bundle X

every MCP tool, core and plugin, carries registry metadata: a canonical dotted id, its heading and sub-heading, a short keyword-first summary and a gate class read off the existing gate sets, with flat names mapping to ids both ways; the 27 writes with no declared gate sit in one pinned allowlist for P2; what clients see on the MCP server is byte-for-byte unchanged

export a session or a project to one crate file you can verify for years and read back without carnivore: byte exact, optionally encrypted with age, copied and verified at a second folder, and marked exported in deep search; a separate share variant is redacted and resumes only as a fork

hold shift and open a session's row menu for restart now: one click kills the running agent and resumes its conversation through the normal restart route, no picker; a pane not measured running opens the normal picker with the reason
in a browser tab, cmd+, (ctrl+, off a Mac) on any Carnivore page opens Carnivore's Settings instead of the browser's, and the shortcuts page lists it

installed themes, plugins, skills and mods in warez now open that kind's own page (search, filters, cards, inspector) instead of a bare list of names, with the item you picked selected, and the warez menu is only as wide as its widest row

menu bar session rows wear a status dot in the status light hues, a paired computer's row opens the Pack computers tab, and a Dock click with the server down opens a small native status window instead of the menu
opening a link to a layout or a session with a page in the fragment, such as /layout/<id>#projects, now keeps that page open instead of dropping to the terminal

pack skill sync fixes: trash what it placed now removes the catalog installs and mirrors it placed and keeps any row it did not remove, a bundle can no longer carry a skill sidecar, the auto update hold ends when the alpha is replaced or unpaired and covers only items actually installed, a copy displaced by a failed install is still reported

pack skill sync leftovers: an uninstalled catalog skill comes back while alpha names it, the preview and matrix know catalog rows, remove everywhere uninstalls a placed one, and existing notification destinations get the pack skills alert tick

pack skill sync now tells you what alpha does: an alert on every computer when alpha changes (with one click back), an alert when an unpaired computer left skills behind (with a two click trash), an alert when a local skill edit was replaced (kept 14 days), and each skill row on a receiver says which computer placed it

pack skill sync, alpha side: the pack's alpha publishes which skills are chosen and their digests, sends changed skills to each computer that is behind, puts a receiver's edited copy back, stops after three tries, never deletes a skill that vanished on alpha, and a new alpha that is behind or differs holds instead of publishing; no screen changes yet

pack skill sync, alpha watcher: the pack's alpha notices an edit inside a synced skill within about three seconds and publishes it, watching folders rather than files so an editor's save-by-rename is seen; no screen changes yet

pack skill sync, owner routes: the pack's alpha can choose which personal skills stay the same on every computer through a dry run and a plan token, resolve a held skill, sync now, and trash what another computer placed; agents get a read only status tool; no screen changes yet

pack skill sync, receiving side: a computer accepts skills only from the pack's alpha, verifies and installs them into its own claude profiles and codex folder, keeps its own built folders and moves what it replaces to the skills trash; nothing is sent yet and no screen changes
removed the uncalled closed-row code from the agents sidebar: the row builder, the closed chip, its styles and strings

scheduled task manager items now sit in the automations sessions tree, as child rows under the session each one wakes (else its project, else unassigned), with small icons to pause or resume, change the time and repeat, and delete behind a confirm; the automations huddle tab and the settings scheduled tasks panel are gone

server routes for the new menu bar menu: Keep Mac Awake (hold the Mac awake whatever the sessions do, kept across restarts), Stand Down (beast mode off, swarm off, scheduler paused in one call, also an MCP tool), debug logging that switches itself back after at most 30 minutes, and a redacted diagnostics bundle that also prints with the server down

settings > advanced > mcp tools groups tools by registry heading then sub-heading instead of the first word of the name; a tool with no sub-heading sits directly under its heading, and app settings is now a filter label rather than a group

several open tabs no longer all fall to the code screen when the shared sign-in expires: when they refresh at the same instant, the ones that lose the race inside the grace window get back the same new tokens the winner got instead of a refusal that wiped the shared sign-in

changes.details: Purging the share plugin ends every live read-only link first. New route: DELETE /api/v1/spectator-links.
changes.summary: share, unread, flow, mcp health, review board and save keep their strings and style guide entries in their own folders, a purge removes every file a plugin declares, and the share dialog can revoke every live link at once

the Task Manager's data lives in carnivore.db as work_ tables, copied once from huddle.db by a verified one-way import at boot; huddle.db stays as a read-only leftover, and scripts/work/work_export.py writes it back for a rollback (#1711)
the conversation backups' chunker, blob codec and pacer moved to core (src/core/blobcodec) so the crate plugin chunks exactly as the backups do; no change in behavior
the menu bar app no longer sends a burst of sign-in code checks at boot, so a code typed right after a restart is not blocked by the verify limit

the menu bar app's launchd log moves from /tmp to ~/Library/Logs/Carnivore (menubar.log and menubar-error.log, folder owner-only); an existing login item is rewritten to the new paths at the next launch and uses them from the next login, and a tracked newsyslog rule rotates them

the menu bar menu is rebuilt: a status header, Need You with routes into the app, Sessions with open, watch, type and attach per session, Phone Access, Keep Mac Awake, Autonomy with Stand Down, and Server & Troubleshoot; while the server is down it counts the agents alive in tmux and offers the survival kit
the new project form asks which computer first and then lists that computer's own launchers; a paired computer that has not been updated shows the agent families and runs its own default launcher

the session contents widget is now session resources, with a library icon: a filter box, folding sections with line counts and scope letters, a details footer with the path and load status, items open in the Files tab, and a local, global, all scope toggle in the title row with the standard icon menu and right-click menu

the skill page matches its mockup more closely: the effect line under each state switch on a narrow pane, paragraph and list spacing in the formatted SKILL.md, an accent outline on the pressed view md and versions buttons, versions with time in words, line counts and each note beside its own version, bold headings in the raw view, and two-up detail tiles on a phone

the skill page's saved versions now keep the note with the version it describes and show line counts, a saved text is checked against the exact bytes you opened, a huge save is refused early, a vanished file says gone, and a skill that is removed and recreated starts with no old versions; starring a skill with spaces or non-ASCII in its name now sticks

the skills page gets a pack tab: pick which personal skills stay the same on every computer, with a check before anything changes, a word and a shape for every computer's state, and a read only view on every computer except alpha

the warez add menu now has add to global and add to project, which opens a list of every registered project by name with the one you are viewing first; a project that already has the item is greyed out

the warez page gets a left menu in place of the filter rail: find in warez, a store group, an installed group whose kinds open to their items and manage them on the right, and a phone first screen with a back bar

the warez phone menu now fits between the title strip and the notice at the bottom, with the search pinned and the list scrolling inside its own box, so the installed rows no longer rest under the notice

the working-on line is removed: the one line ai label above the prompt bar saying what each live session is working on is gone, with the summarize plugin, its settings panel, token budget, routes (/ai-summaries/*, /sessions/{id}/working-on), the working_on fields of the sessions list, the dated bullets of the conversations route and the session_bullets_get MCP tool; the sessions page panel and rows no longer show it. The owner ruled it killed. ai_summaries.db is left on disk untouched
usage stats is no longer a plugin: its one on/off switch is in settings, advanced, statistics, and your current choice carries over unchanged

warez installed pages: the menu is exactly as wide as its rows, picking an item inside a page selects it in the address and the menu, filter bars lay out in one clean row or a deliberate wrap, plugin tabs no longer overlap their counts, the phone pages lose the blank band and the clipped skills toolbar, and the menu's state words follow a switch at once
warez installed polish: a plugin card's gear now moves the address and the menu to that plugin, the left menu never clips its find field's hint, and the embedded plugin pane's four tabs fit at 1440
a card dealt to a sleeping agent now wakes it right away even when the computer is pegged, instead of waiting for a slot until the load drops
a computer can only apply a bundle or archive it uploaded itself: naming a blob another paired computer uploaded is refused with blob_not_yours and logged
a folder named with tmux format text (#{...} or #(...)) is taken literally as a session's start directory: new-session -c and respawn-pane -c both go through the one escape, tmux_quote.literal

a fresh install no longer asks for the current session when the live session list answers empty, so no page load logs a 404; the terminal key bar waits for the string layer before it logs an error; tmdevtools keeps its two strings in its own catalog slice; the rail harness fixture no longer names the flow plugin's string keys

a loadout member pinned to an older version is checked against its own publisher release signature and the revocation list before anything is fetched, the same check a direct install of that version runs; a revoked or tampered version is refused with its own reason and the rest of the set still installs
a message to a sleeping agent whose body takes longer than 90 seconds to wake is now queued and delivered once the body is up, instead of dropped with an error

a one-time notice that installs are reported to the carnivore catalog (item id, version, account id), why, and that there is no switch, acknowledged once per user across devices; settings account gets an install reports group listing every field sent, checked against the real reporter by a test
a project made in the new project wizard on a paired computer is named what you typed, and the paired computer runs its own folder checks (typed folder, no far-side browse yet)
a project's chosen color now draws a thin outline around its whole drawer block over a faint ground in that color, instead of tinting the folder and name; no color looks as before

a project's drawer block gets 5px of air inside its outline, every project without a chosen color draws a gray 56/56/56 block, the custom color picker opens a popover with a preview, R G B fields and an OK button, and its swatch wears a color wheel icon

a question card for a peer paired with no label now shows the short id instead of the whole raw key and its chip shrinks to fit; the drawer's awake and sleeping filters follow the phone line without a reload; the elite detail pane credits the publisher without the publisher/name id line
a question from a paired computer names it (studio) instead of its raw peer id, and hovering the open questions slide-out while the rail is hidden no longer brings the rail and menu back

a theme opened in the warez store now shows the same inspector as the themes page (large plate, id, source, developer and version, interface and terminal palette, ratings) with add and try it as its action row; skills, mods and plugins keep their detail pane
an agent that already exists always wakes when you message it, even when the computer is pegged; only starting a brand-new agent still waits for the load to drop
an openrouter connection can now generate images through the shared ai layer, so skill card images route to it, come back as image bytes and record their cost

an own crate can now carry the project folder's files too: a checkbox in the export dialog (off by default, own copies only) adds the folder as a project home, with links recorded never followed, a fixed skip list for node_modules, venv and build output, the git branch, commit and uncommitted changes, and a preview that lists every skipped folder with its size

an own crate now carries the review boards linked to the project's tasks (and their drafts), and every plugin's stores come from the data it declares in its manifest: the preview lists each one with its carried count and bytes or the reason it is left out, an unset folder setting is listed and never blocks, and a plugin that keeps data without declaring it makes the export refuse instead of passing quietly
beast mode now approves an agent's project archive and restore requests instead of asking you; deletes, renames, credentials and settings still ask
beast mode now approves an agent's renames, moves, automation writes and stops of a session that is mid-work instead of asking you; deletes and adding or removing computers still ask
closed sessions are back in the agents sidebar, behind a new show closed sessions tick in the view menu that is on by default and kept per device class (desktop and phone)
config.json and its backup are written owner-only (0600) from the first byte, and an older world-readable config.json or backup copy is tightened once at startup

conversation backups own their vault location as a plugin setting shown and checked in the settings pane (copied once from the old config value, nothing moved), and any plugin can mark a folder for the vault: review boards and drafts are backed up hourly with git history, listed with their size, and restore into a new folder beside the original

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): a crate made with the project's files restores them into a new folder named for the project and the crate date, never into the project's own folder; a link is re-created only when it stays inside that folder (a chain of links that climbs out is listed, not made), the uncommitted patch and git facts are kept in the receipt and never applied, and the tick to work in the restored copy makes that folder the new project's root

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): a share crate can now be restored: its redacted conversations are filed in the new folder's Claude folder and each session comes back asleep, and its first wake resumes as a fork so the redacted copy is never continued in place

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): restoring a crate into a different folder now works end to end: conversation folders are renamed for the new location so every restored session still resumes, the project and session folders and the paths in the restored rows follow, the old folder's deleted-project mark stays while the new one's is cleared, a reopen-journal entry of a restored session moves with it while other sessions' entries stay put, and a project that already exists here at another folder is followed instead of duplicated; a session crate now also names the project it came from, so no project has to be picked

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): restoring a crate into an install that already has its own data is now exact: ids that clash are never reused and everything that points at a restored row follows it, a row already here wins and is listed, a shorter local conversation file grows to the crate's longer copy after its old bytes are saved (and a fault puts them back), a conversation file with different bytes keeps its session out (skip conflicts restores the rest), a session id already used by another conversation gets a new one, a conversation another session already holds is not duplicated, and the apply checks again for a running session before it touches the first file

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): restoring a crate now brings back the project's Task Manager and the data around it: items, messages, groups, history and attached files land under the project's list here (a list that already has items gets the new ones in a group named for the crate), nothing is due afterwards (reminders paused, automations switched off with no next run, queued messages expired), bookmarks, attention history, automations and chart notes follow the new ids and folder, and the drawer layout is merged in without changing what is already there

crate import engine, not reachable yet (no route or job starts an import on this line): restoring a crate now puts back other plugins' data too: a review board that is not here is placed in its restored task's folder and relinked, a board already here wins and the crate's copy is kept beside it in a hidden folder, a plugin store with no folder set here is kept in the restore receipt instead of failing, and a store marked keep never loses an entry

crate import groundwork, no visible change: one no-clobber file placer shared by the vault restore and the crate extract, the Task Manager list import body callable inside a caller's transaction, the project row insert and its undo split out of create, the session adoption skipping a live set, a prefix path mapping with a per-session journal rebase, a writer-origin mark on crates this install exported, and the frozen v1.1 golden fixtures

design ratchets back toward green: 15 components and the media lightbox sheet move into a cascade layer, pack rows and the notes cell use the spacing tokens, review board and skills names reveal their full text only when cut off, the drawer card header test follows the menu-only gear
drag the rows of the drawer's menu tab to put them in your own order (long-press and drag on a phone, Alt+Up and Alt+Down from the keyboard); the order is shared across your devices

eleven session routes (timeline, timeline peek, move-folder, save points, latest-lines, usage, contents, huddle dnd) now have a peer forward-table row: refused or local on purpose, so the federation table test is green again

elite access gets its file area: every file in the index as numbered rows with real install counts and update and installed markers, every menu letter wired to the catalog's own filters and sorts, a top ten from measured installs, search, and an offline banner over the cached listing

elite access gets its right rail: the FILE_ID.DIZ pane for the file under the bar (rating, installs, versions, trust and grade meters, works with, comments and the install link) with a sheet on a phone, the tagged pane with D, U and C batches, plus and equals to add or try through the product's own install, update and try flows, shift+M to comment and a keys help overlay

elite access plays the modem sound again, always on: the sound option stays removed (no toggle, no Alt+M, no session block, the stored choice is no longer read), the id line under item titles stays gone

elite access polish: the file_id.diz carries the modem sound checkbox, the help overlay lists the everywhere keys, the prompt echoes all files, the page ground matches, and space on a focused button and option keys typed in a field no longer fire board shortcuts
elite access remembers your modem sound choice on every device and your last call: the boot and welcome lines name your previous visit, the n key lists the uploads newer than it and each wears a star

elite access: alt+l replays the logo again, the file list sits on the same rows as the mockup (no stray blank line above the first file), and opening it no longer freezes the page for over a second so the dial-up text shows at once

enter on a skill name now opens it on the embedded warez skills page, a skill's page has a regenerate image button (disabled with the reason until an image model is chosen), and a removed image route can never fall back to the default image model

every branch of the new claude project menu reads Next until the last step, then Create Project; the remote folder hint says whether the folder is made or must exist, and a paired computer's folder is no longer prefilled with a guess

every plugin now declares the data it keeps (databases, folders, files) in its carnivore.json, with who may carry it in an export, so export and inventory can find a plugin's stores without a fixed table in core

every widget now has a validated contract record (hosts, sizes, the data it reads, fixtures, builtin or declarative), the widget schema refuses any non-builtin widget that is not declarative, and a widget gate runs each record's fixture scenarios through the widget lab harness in every declared host and size under at least two themes and writes a pass or fail record that a submission must hold
image, video, audio, speech and transcription calls made to an explicit target now log their feature id, so the AI call log and the AI spend view attribute skill card image spend to skills.card_art

installing a new version no longer renames the running carnivore app: only its contents are swapped, so macos privacy grants (full disk access, removable volumes) stay put, and the previous version is kept as a rollback outside applications

move a session out of its temp folder: POST /sessions/{session_uuid}/move-folder carries a ses_ folder's files (backed up first, verified, a same-name file refuses) into an existing project or a new folder, restarts the pane there in the same tmux session as a resume of the same conversation, and writes the folder and project together; the transcript stays where claude filed it; MCP tool session_folder_move wraps the same route
pack skills tab: one row per skill with an icon for each family, a sticky header row in the ledger label style, and a confirm sheet that talks only about the skill you are changing
picking a row in the sidebar menu with a mouse no longer makes the menu close and then slide back out: the pointer leaving as the drawer closes is a retract, not a new peek

plugin spec fixes: a purge keeps the stores a plugin declares kept and the price names them (save's old restore point tree is never deleted by a purge); data entries gain purge, default, state_path and a backup destination role whose folder is refused when symlinked or synced and warned when on the same disk; every served route is declared; review boards warn when their checkout has no commits or no remote

plugins now carry a carnivore.json sidecar that is checked against the new extension contract schemas when the app starts, one permission list feeds the manifest parser and the consent risk levels, and a downloadable plugin shows its real author instead of its publisher

providers panel: the smallest view is the all accounts total alone (5h and 7d on one line), a click on the header title steps the density, and the glance tiles are a fourth view (new synced fold key ledger_glance)

restoring a crate works: the restore button now starts the restore as a job with progress, writes the project, sessions (all asleep), conversation files and records only after a full check of the crate and only for the plan you saw, and leaves a receipt you can read again; an app stop before the records are saved removes what it placed, and after they are saved it finishes on the next start; agents can ask for a restore through the approval inbox, but never for an encrypted crate and never with the 'I made this crate here' tick

scheduled task manager items show again on the redesigned automations page, filed under their project and session below the table, with small icons to pause or resume, change the time and repeat, and delete behind a confirm
settings > mcp server lists the trusted proxy addresses and lets you add one (checked as an exact ip address, duplicates and junk refused in plain words) or remove one
settings ai: a model that outputs images is offered for image routes, so an openrouter image model can be picked for skill card images

skill card briefs now run on your chat default with no extra setup, cover every installed skill by reading its SKILL.md when the description is empty, fit three lines without a cut and fill in as a model becomes available; with no model the card shows the description's first sentence or the skill file's first sentence, never just the name

skill card briefs read only the first line of the model's reply and are shortened up to twice, so a brief is always a whole sentence; when it still does not fit the card shows the description's first sentence and tries again later, and old briefs are cleaned up

skill cards show a one sentence AI summary that fits three lines when a text model is chosen for skill card summaries in Settings > AI, cached per skill text and written off the page load; with none chosen the card shows the plain description

the Settings screen has a plugins heading at the bottom of its rail with one entry per enabled plugin that has settings, each drawing the plugin's own settings form, deep linked as #settings/plugin/<id>, following plugins turned on or off live, and found by the Settings search through field labels, hints, keywords and the plugin name

the Warez page has an [ELITE ACCESS] button that opens a BBS-themed view: a modem dial-up login, the logo, a node box, last callers from this computer's ledger and a main menu (the file list follows in later slices)
the agents drawer lists the projects inside each company, and inside orphaned projects, A to Z by name (case-insensitive, p2 before p10)

the automations and sessions page buttons and the timeline rows wear the shared oc-btn family at their old sizes, menu labels show their full text on hover only while cut off, the resting-row effort pause has its own stylesheet

the backups storage panel now lists each backed-up plugin folder with its size, restore points and last backup time, and restores a chosen point into a new folder beside the live one after an inline confirm; a settings warning such as same disk as your transcripts is now kept whole when saved (code, message, field and full detail, in settings_warnings) and shows under its field, and no longer replaces the plugin's permission warnings

the base folder and parent-folder refusal now ignores letter case and accent spelling (composed or decomposed), a refused folder is caught before the new session starts so no stray session is left behind, and a paired computer's project hand-off onto a base folder is refused cleanly instead of failing

the catalog index key can now be retired in the field: the app pins a spare index key (a fail-closed placeholder until Alex generates it) and honors a carnivore-index-key-revoked-v1 statement signed by that spare, fetched beside the index, after which only the spare may sign an index, across restarts; the statement signs the spare's first serial, which becomes its rollback floor so the spare can continue a high live series, and a release DMG build marked requireSpareIndexKey (from the 1.0 release on) refuses to run while the spare is still the placeholder

the crate plugin can now preview restoring a crate (POST /imports/plan and the crate_import_preview tool): whether this computer wrote it, which project and folder it lands in, which conversation folders and files would be written and which clash, how every table would be handled, what is never restored, and the live sessions and open offers that block it; the preview writes nothing and ends in a fingerprint the restore will have to quote

the crate plugin has a restore dialog: a recorded crate's restore button (in the crates settings and on a project's crates group) opens a preview of what restoring would do, where it would land (the same folders, or a new folder with the suggested one a click away), who wrote the crate, every conversation and how it would resume, and what blocks it, in plain sentences; the restore button appears only on a plan that can go ahead and sends the plan that was shown

the custom project color picker is now one box: a saturation and brightness square, a hue bar, a preview, R G B fields and an eyedropper, with cancel and ok right under them, so after you drag the color around you can see where to confirm it
the first time you open warez you land in elite access; the [elite access] button is gone and a gray pi in the bottom-right corner of the warez menu opens it

the image picker for an openrouter connection lists the models its image route serves (from its image models listing, such as openai/gpt-image-2) and no longer offers text and image chat models that fail there

the mcp on-demand surface (the mcp on demand plugin, its three discover, describe and execute tools and the skills loader) is parked after the a/b run and removed from the app; the flat tool list is the only surface, and the surface column in the mcp event log stays, always a
the new project wizard browses a paired computer's own folders (under its home and projects folder) when that computer runs this version or newer; an older one keeps the typed folder and says why
the new project wizard on a paired computer asks for the folder there so the project is named what you typed, lists the computer once, and its buttons read Next then Create Project

the one-time installs are reported modal and the installs are reported consent lines on the install sheet and item detail are removed on Alex's instruction; install reporting itself and the settings install reports group are unchanged

the pack settings document is now signed by the computer that changed it, and only a change signed by the alpha a computer follows can move the alpha there, so a compromised paired computer can no longer make itself alpha or plant skills by sending an edited document; older and replayed versions and tampered fields are refused, the alpha's first signed version is trusted on first use, unsigned changes are refused after that with an alert, and pack settings are changed on alpha; after the security review the refused-change alert only explains (no button that adopts the change), a computer signs only its own edits (a document main sends on a join is never signed by the joiner), and the first trusted signer is the alpha a computer held before any unsigned change arrived, so a planted unsigned change cannot lock the real alpha out

war room wall is one uniform grid of equal tiles that fills the window, each project outlined in its color, a stable sidebar order, and a 2.5x hover peek; the wall refreshes every second, stretching toward 5 s as sessions pile up (at most 8 screen grabs a second), and a session with no readable screen shows a card; the page no longer re-flows from another surface's height

war room wall shows live screens of sessions on paired computers, batched per computer over the link; a computer on an older release shows a paired-computer-needs-an-update card until it comes back updated, an unreachable one keeps its last picture

warez gate 10 now binds the AI review to the folder digest the row claims (other bytes are undetermined, nothing spent) and the review job records that digest; a gate submit must carry every gate once (a missing gate is undetermined, a duplicate is refused, differing digests are refused) and only a complete set can be overridable

warez gate runner CLI for the ops workflows: a clean-room subcommand for gate 11 over one in-process host (now a production module), poll --max --json for a job matrix, materialize turns downloaded pending objects into a safe gate folder, and submit requires gates 1 to 12 and re-scans the report for credential shapes before posting

warez publish bot support in the hosted intake: POST /v1/submissions/{id}/published (claim owner only, idempotent per merge sha), and a long-lived scoped bot token (cbt_, stored as sha256, admin mint and revoke) valid only on the approved and publishing listing, claim, release and published; secret detector for the cbt_ prefix; hosted API not deployed
warez static gates scan binary members for secrets and fetch only from registry hosts

changes.details: Both tools take account and always_use_account like session_create; a bad account is refused before the owner is asked and the error names the launchable ids. No account sent keeps the saved pin, else the active account.

a layout cell under another cell, beside a full height cell, can be enlarged: dead trailing rows are trimmed on load and on every edit, and dragging a seam up takes space from the rows the cell above stands on

a packaged plugin can read redacted MCP health data (process names, server names and transports, link states) through three host methods behind one permission; the measuring moved into core and runs only while the plugin is on
a page's rows draw no menu button: the Sessions page's session rows, project headings and automation rows lose their kebab, and their menu is the row's right click and Shift+F10 in the one item menu

a plugin UI document with a list or dict where a route, tool name, tone or status belongs is refused as a bad document (stale fallback applies) instead of a server error; a trailing newline in a bind pointer and a true schema are refused
a plugin ui document's data block no longer carries URL schemes into bound text: only whole id-shaped strings (adopted:, plugin:, remote:) skip the scheme check, in both validators

a plugin view that navigates itself is unmounted and loses the bridge, the overlay follows terminals that move, keyboard focus returns to the terminal after a click on a pet, and the view file route no longer blocks on a pipe
a portal override records the approver's login, falling back to the GitHub login linked to the account, so the publish worker no longer releases an email admin's override unpublished

a running third-party plugin can show a settings view, a status chip on its row and detail, and a bar indicator as declarative documents the app re-validates and draws itself inside a frame that names the plugin and marks it third-party outside the plugin's box
a skill installed by Pack skill sync now reads consent taken via pack skill sync from another computer, instead of one click

a third-party plugin can declare event subscriptions in its manifest and is then started at boot and never idle-stopped, an event reaches a stopped plugin through its first-use start, an idle plugin is revoked, paused on an expired index and switched off by safe mode like a running one, and a burst of calls reads memory and CPU at most once a second

a third-party plugin can ship its own drawn view (a panel or a transparent overlay for pixel pets) that runs in a sandboxed iframe with no network, storage, cookies or parent access, and talks to the app only over a nonce-checked bridge to its declared routes

a third-party plugin that is on starts at its first call instead of at switch-on, is stopped after ten idle minutes without counting a crash, and its resource watchdog reads memory and CPU in one ps call, every second only during calls and the first 30 seconds
a third-party plugin whose update fails after it was stopped is started again on its old files; the hourly index check follows a plugin switched on mid-wait within the hour

admin page: passkey sign in (email code kept as the secondary), first passkey enrolment with the operator's one-time code, a passkey list with add and remove, and the page now calls https://api.carnivore.ai/v1 directly so it can run as its own site at admin.carnivore.ai; deploy-site.sh and customHttp.yml for the Amplify app

an analytics chart card narrower or shorter than its renderer floor now shrinks to its title, headline figure and caption (the tokens breakdown is kept whole or dropped whole) instead of the not-available plate, and a card still waiting for its chart list keeps its last title and shows the loading state instead of chart definition unavailable
an old archive import approval card that waits through a server restart still finds its preview when approved, instead of resolving refused with "fingerprint is required"

an uninstall script at carnivore.ai/uninstall.sh and an uninstall help page: it lists what it removes, asks first (--yes and --dry-run), stops the app, login items, server and tmux sessions, deletes the app, its folders and keychain items, and keeps your projects and Claude logins

aws-runner R8 fixes: the claude binary and every pip install are pinned by sha256, the download-check test names each file, and deploy-runner.sh re-reads projects per pass, saves prior rule, policy and concurrency state, asks before applying and fails loudly on a permission error (epic 2063)
beast mode stays armed across a restart or a crash until you turn it off
bot_token.py remint: mints the three ops bot tokens from a passkey admin session, smoke-calls them, stores them in the ops repo environment secrets over stdin, then revokes the old ids
catalog card art is composed like the in-app card art: the frame fills the whole 16:9 banner, with no empty dark side fields asked for and no sides check in the vision judge
claiming a pending revocation now answers status revoked instead of publishing

cron reads the nth weekday of a month (2#3 is the third tuesday), and a new route turns a sentence like every third tuesday at 5 pm into a cron through the connected AI for confirmation, saving nothing

dead catalog code removed: the unmounted GitHub and email sign in panels with their device flow reader, the unrendered scope chips, theme swatch rows and detail panes for mods and plugins, plus the catalog strings, style guide rows and tests that only they used (site review slices 6 and 7, item 1148); no visible change

decision records and docs for the warez and sidecar work: the reversals of decisions 1, 7 and 20, Joe's calls 2 and 6 and the nyedis handle, the retirement of docs/warez/05 slices 6 to 9 and 13 to 16, the pipeline as built and switched off, and catalog entries for the third-party plugins switch, sideload, the view frame, the admin portal and author status

dependency security floors: pillow 13.0.0, PyJWT 2.14, anyio 4.14.2, certifi 2026.10.19, starlette 1.3.1, python-multipart 0.0.30, cryptography 48.0.1 in the app server, urllib3 2.8.0 in the app server and dev scripts, and axios 1.20 in the macOS app
every finished automation run now carries a plain title and a one-line summary, built from what the run recorded with no AI text
gate 11 clean room stubs guest_account keychain read and write so the host keychain is never touched
gate 11 compares claude --version with the pin before installing; a mismatch or unreadable version is undetermined
gate 11 residue check allows Claude Code's own config and backup files and still fails any other leftover

hosted admin passkey: authenticator data with the extension data flag (a security key's credProtect answer) is accepted when a strict CBOR text keyed map follows with no trailing byte, on enrolment and sign in; trailing bytes with the flag clear are still refused
hosted catalog API accepts AWS IAM runner callers on a dedicated runner route (fixed role table, own account only, no bearer token), inert until the gateway route exists
hosted catalog API puts an id-only runner event on the EventBridge bus after a submission is received, regated, approved or revoked, inert until RUNNER_EVENT_BUS is set
hosted catalog API runner identity matches the caller ARN with a full match, so a userArn with a trailing newline is refused
hosted catalog API task runner_sweep re-emits runner events for stale received, gating, approved, publishing and revoked rows, at most 10 a pass, inert until the schedule exists

hosted catalog API: admin passkey sign in (WebAuthn routes, operator-gated enrolment, passkey admin session, CORS allow-list for the admin site, passkey cutover flag), all inert until ADMIN_SITE_ORIGIN is set

hosted catalog deploy carries RUNNER_EVENT_BUS and PUBLISH_ENABLED forward and schedules the 10 minute runner sweep, the gateway gains the IAM-authorized runner route, and the runner identity logs the IAM block's key names only

hot reads reuse one database connection per thread instead of opening a new one each time: the Task Manager's seat, do-not-disturb, schedule and send-pick reads, the asleep list read, and the label and identity lookups no longer parse the schema on every call
huddle: carnivore's view, the hidden third list view, is removed with its flag, setting option and strings (a stored one still reads as by group)

idle CPU waste batch: deep search cache checked once at boot, cached automations pause flag, MCP tools/list plugin state cache, skill-fire scan skips unchanged transcripts, vault lane gate, Pack roster on a push topic
layout column dividers keep going into the next cell once a neighbour hits its minimum width, and dropping a cell into a new row or onto a row no longer resets the other sizes to equal
layout dividers are freeform: they follow the pointer pixel for pixel with no snapping, a small cell can always be dragged bigger, one minimum size applies everywhere, and empty strip rows fold away

master reds cleared: the no-delete wording guard records every surface that really deletes, the menu conformance ratchet records the pack roster sort facet, and a test pins that features check refuses what render refuses

one listing push pass builds the live listing and the asleep list once: the Task Manager's ports reuse the pass's rows and one light asleep read, the wake clock is shared, folder themes are cached, a Task Manager write wakes the listing only when a row would change, and the scheduled read starts from the trigger table

plugin text in the declarative UI is pinned inert by a render test, the status chip and the bar tooltip carry the host's third-party mark, the bar re-keys a plugin's watcher after an update or reinstall, the client counts a document's size exactly as the server does, and the style guide bundle fetches nothing signed out
project colors are hex only: older projects that still held a color name now hold the matching fixed hex, and the project route and the mcp tool refuse a color name with a clear error

purging a third-party plugin whose Keychain, egress or activity delete fails now answers cplug_purge_incomplete and keeps its name and install id held, so purging again retries instead of orphaning the data

records for the move of the warez gate, publish and revoke runners from GitHub Actions to AWS (epic 2063): decision entry, docs/warez/aws-runner.md, and the unused bot_token.py remint subcommand removed

release-signer tests load the handler under a unique module name and use monkeypatch for the env; the signer's list scope and revoked-facts read are tested; bot callers of the submission list never receive the submitter block

search results: names, prompts and all results are just the result with no buttons and one click opens it, the context mode alone shows every action button at once, the similar terms row is the context mode's only, nothing is drawn on hover, and the no-match line names the typed text and follows the mode

server log warning noise cleared: the unpinned spare index key is logged once per process, built-in themes use the current radius tokens, and subagent bookkeeping lines (fork-context-ref, api-request) are accepted by the shape contract
sidebar search results no longer grow, recolor or scroll as the mouse passes over them: a hover only tints a row, and a row opens to four lines with its actions only by arrow key or click

sidebar search: each mode searches only its own kind again (names lists agents only), a fourth mode, all, gives agents and conversations together; one click on a hit opens it, and / focuses the box from anywhere but a field or the terminal
take it from another computer: alpha's owner can pull a skill only that computer has, or an edit there worth keeping, into alpha from the Pack skills tab
task manager mark ii gets a subtasks tab (forks with title, status and owner; agents list them with task_manager_tasks_list item) and the review checklist as tickable checkboxes on the action tab

task rules: an unread agent info puts its task in needs you until you mark it read or its status changes, every status change adds a line to the task's conversation (who, from, to, when), a collapsed waiting row shows when it should be over, and the agent guide and tool descriptions say how to handle tasks (guide rev 107)

the AWS runner's definitions land: five CodeBuild buildspecs, the gate state machine, one IAM policy and trust per role, pinned downloads, the deploy and config scripts, and a test that proves the clean room reaches no secret and each secret has one reader (epic 2063, aws-runner R8)

the alert action, the beast arm and the conversation fork calls moved out of their components into the alerts store, the beast control store and a fork route client; the remaining hard-coded labels in the terminal search, session tools, copy output sheet, paste fallback, header menu and a few more surfaces are read from the message catalog (site review slice 15)

the app mints and trusts the first-party handle carnivore while nyedis stays trusted until the re-signed releases are live; an installed nyedis row relabels only for a trusted carnivore twin at its own version and digest; hosted ratings and other item-keyed rows get a copy-then-delete re-key script

the automations screen reads the base design tokens for every spacing, height, corner, tracking and line height it drew raw, its row and pane menu buttons are the shared bare icon button, and its two fold chevrons are the shared fold chevron

the carnivore/mcphealth sidecar package now reports the same per-row mcp_health as the compiled-in plugin: adopted sessions and server names with colons ride in the ui document data block, and mcp.config rows carry a redacted alive flag so a stdio server whose process is gone reads down
the catalog Lambda build pins every vendored distribution, the transitive pycparser included, so two builds of a commit install the same dependency versions
the catalog batch sign step signs the publisher-key delegation with the releases in one passphrase prompt, the pr step carries it in the publisher record, and the batch tooling accepts the cplug kind

the clean-room isolation self-check runs its inside probe with the system python3 behind the setpriv uid drop, because uid 65534 cannot load the CodeBuild image's pyenv python under /root and gate 11 answered isolation_unverified for every build
the companies list reads each hero art failure note once and the theme script digest hashes a theme folder once, both served from memory until the file's stat changes or its writer runs

the design base gains its list and row, toolbar and empty, loading and error state components, shown under every theme in the style guide; the automations list draws its rows, toolbar and empty states with them, so a selected row wears the base selected layer and run now with the row menu shows on hover, focus or selection (always on a phone)

the desktop app updates itself from the public releases: a settings block (running version, status, update now, check now) and an update automatically switch that is off by default, which downloads in the background and restarts at a quiet moment when on; the install stops the server first

the gate state machine mints its own run id with States.UUID in a first Pass state, because an EventBridge-started execution name is 73 characters with an underscore and the buildspecs refused it as RUN before any claim

the hosted catalog API can take a published submission back with a written reason (audit row first), lists pending revocations for the publish bot and records when the signed revocation is merged, and the admin portal gets a one-click revoke with a required reason and a revoked tab
the hosted release route gives back a claimed revocation without moving it off revoked and pending, and revocation-published stores the revocation merge sha for the admin row

the main tab strip's close and skull key and the left rail's close key are drawn by the one shared key (a close slot on the key), so a tab and a rail key close and arm the skull the same way (wrapper packages K-3 and K-4, item 1147); nothing looks different

the mcphealth host port is withdrawn on every stop (uninstall, update, sideload stop, revocation, index expiry), command names passed to the sidecar are a whitelist, and the catalog lists the moved monitor

the mcphealth sidecar package folder (packages/cplugs/mcphealth/), unsigned: it re-implements the plugin on the three A13 host methods and judges the same per-row mcp_health as the compiled-in plugin for the same seed
the menu bar menu gets Uninstall Carnivore... as the first Uninstall row: a typed UNINSTALL gate, then the public uninstall script runs detached from a private copy
the one-time conversation backfill script is retired and kept on a git branch

the packaged app now accepts only the two official release feeds for updates (stable and the beta channel); any other feed url, from the environment or the config, is refused as an invalid feed and no update check starts
the per computer app update controls now show on the live Pack page: each computer's overview tab has an app update section with its version, status, update now and the auto update switch

the publish bot can sign a version revocation with the delegated release key and merge it (built and disabled), and the app honours a version revocation signed by a delegated key for community items only, never for a first-party or reserved handle

the publish view lists a mod folder (a plugin folder whose hooks/hooks.json carries modules) as a mod, checks it locally by the catalog's mod rules, and sends it as kind mod; a plugin folder with hooks is still refused as a plugin

the publish worker commits the gate's stored AI review as reviews/<handle>/<name>/<version>.json with the row's override block, releases a row whose review is missing or bound to other bytes, and failed releases are written to stderr and not listed as released

the publish worker no longer lists a row whose release failed as released, a failed claim release prints the id and error class only, and an overridden review carries the approver login the catalog check names

the publish worker's signer now checks the claim owner and kind, an aborted run closes its PR and deletes its branch, a merge whose answer was lost is checked before rows are released, and /published is retried

the publish worker, release signer, release key generator and sha-pinned auto-merge are built and switched off (PUBLISH_ENABLED stays false); sign_plan takes a signer and delegations and open_pr takes an App token

the release-signer Lambda for the AWS warez runner: parses release and revoke statements, checks each against the API's row, signs with the release key held only there; the signer role may list rows and verify scope reads revoked rows

the schedules list tool no longer fails when a schedule is tagged to a session that is asleep: the Task Manager reads the asleep list without an owner request, never waking anyone, and a tag naming an asleep session resolves the same way from an MCP call

the sessions page draws its list, session rows, filter bar, tags, fold chevrons and empty states with the design base: rows are the base row at the roomy height with a hairline and the base selected layer, the open or wake button and the menu show on hover, focus or selection (always on a phone), and spacing and font sizes read tokens

the stat tiles, the KPI card and the analytics chart cards are drawn by two shared base components, StatTile and ChartFrame, that share one side inset with the widget header title, which fixes a range label printing over the headline figure and a clipped figure at the one-unit floor
the terminal tab menu keeps search terminal, edit layout and remove widget; extend a row and pull back a row are back in the widget menu in normal view
the ultracode mark lights on the toggle sentence and stays lit through the picker's "Ultracode on" suffix on claude 2.1.306 and later; a plain effort sentence still clears it
the update proof keeps its scratch home when the updater relaunches the app, through a validated marker file read at startup

the war room modal is drawn by the shared modal frame (a terminal keeps Tab and its own Escape) with its header from a one-tab zone, the widget settings form wears the shared anchored popup frame (Escape closes it, focus goes back), and the dialog scan now carries a documented per-file opt-out for the four dialogs that are not modals (wrapper package T-2, item 1147)
the warez clean room counts a tls failure wrapped in a urlerror on the build fetch as an open wall, closed only for a known no-route failure
the warez clean room counts an http error or tls failure on the build fetch as an open wall, measures build walls in any codebuild build, and drops author code with no-new-privs
the warez clean room drops author code to an unprivileged user as root and measures its network walls before running anything; an open or unmeasured wall leaves gate 11 undetermined
the warez publish and revoke commands, a GitHub App token limited to the catalog repo and a release-signer Lambda client, all off unless PUBLISH_ENABLED is exactly 1 and the code default allows

the warez runner client signs hosted api requests with AWS SigV4 when CARNIVORE_CATALOG_AUTH=iam, sends no bearer token in that mode and refuses to send anything without AWS credentials (epic #2063, slice R4)

update a paired computer's Carnivore app from the Pack page: each computer row shows its app version and update status, an update now button and its auto update switch (off unless that computer turned it on); a computer too old for this reads as update it by hand once; the app_update MCP tools do the same

updating an installed third-party plugin stops it before the swap and asks for consent again before it runs; a revoked release or publisher key, or an expired catalog index, stops a running third-party plugin within one index refresh, and the index is checked hourly while one is on
warez gate 1 checks kind, paths and caps without the reserved-handle rule, so first-party items (carnivore, external) pass it; handle ownership stays with gate 4
warez gate 2 compares a native manifest name with the sidecar id only for plugins and mods; a theme's theme.json name is its display name, so the 16 catalog themes no longer fail sidecar agreement
warez gate 2 validates first-party items against L1 plus the item overlay, so scripted first-party themes pass
warez gate 4 requires the catalog releases/ folder; a missing folder or an unreadable statement is undetermined, never a pass

warez gate 9 now fails a fetching runner it cannot pin-check (npm x, flags before exec, uv tool run, deno, docker), any registry or index flag on a launch command, and any npm_config_ or UV_ env key, so the pinned-and-hashed package is the one that runs
warez gates 2 and 8 fail a sidecar whose version or license disagrees with the native manifest
warez gates 3 and 6: a policy skill_scripts flag lets a first-party skill carry scripts/ and its shebangs stay advisory; third party unchanged

warez gates hardening: the report re-scan also refuses the literal value of the catalog token or the review key, and the hosted report and file reads answer 503 on any store error but a missing object instead of 'no report'

warez review and clean-room jobs take --static-results and run only when gates 1 to 9 passed over the same folder digest; a missing document, a failed or absent static gate or another digest is undetermined (static_results_missing, static_gates_not_passed, static_digest_mismatch) before any budget spend, API call or install, so a folder holding a secret never reaches the reviewer
warez runner: the clean-room isolation self-check now measures wall 1 by raw IP connects from the build and wall 4 by uid, /proc/1/environ and root-owned directory probes behind the uid drop
warez submit refuses any results file whose digest is missing or not equal to the row's folder digest; the review job always writes its digest

warez test runner can hold an install, test an update from an older version (--update-from) and release a hold, through the app's real install and update routes; its tests keep off the real hold records
a 204 answer's empty body is read before authFetch returns, so the activity report is no longer cancelled unread (net::ERR_ABORTED) on every page load

a Task Manager widget that holds the all projects read no longer releases and re-takes it every time the data paints, so the all widget keeps its rows beside a session widget; the crate and save plugin manifests declare their web surfaces

a burst of output no longer drops the terminal connection: a viewer that falls behind has its queued output dropped and gets one resync frame plus a fresh capture of the screen on the same socket, with no reconnect notice; the 4429 close stays as the fallback when the capture fails (#2352)
a carnivore link no longer adopts an unbound tmux session, the hotkey default is no longer grabbed before the preference is read, and the link docs now say a link starts the app

a developer-sideloaded sidecar plugin view that declares the panel surface now shows up as a widget in the widget drawer and the home grid, running its own interactive page in the sandboxed view frame (#2379)

a faster keystroke path exists for the terminal: one persistent tmux control client types keys instead of spawning tmux per keystroke; it is on by default, and CARNIVORE_CONTROL_INPUT=0 turns it off and keeps the old per-keystroke path

a node test guards the port seams of the desktop shell: no new Library/ path literal, no call to security, every app.dock use guarded; the release DMG architecture now lives in macOS/release-arch.json, read by the site pin check and the publish script

a page load sends about 65 REST reads instead of about 158: during the first 8 seconds a repeat read of one URL joins the read already in flight or takes a copy of an answer that settled under 1.5 seconds ago, and a write forgets its own resource family (#2348)

a page tab strip keeps its selected tab in view by scrolling only itself sideways, so the Task Manager Mark II list in the opened or detailed state no longer jumps to its bottom on load and on every update
a release build reuses an engine payload tree already built from exactly the same lock, recipe, pins and arch instead of rebuilding it, and CARNIVORE_PAYLOAD_REBUILD=1 forces a rebuild
a terminal pane keeps 5000 scrollback rows instead of 50000, about a tenth of the buffer memory, and scrolling to the top loads older history from tmux 2500 lines at a time (#2384)

a tmux client whose major.minor differs from the server already running on the socket is no longer allowed to list silently wrong: Carnivore keeps using the binary that matches the live server, and when none matches the listing answers a named version_skew error naming both versions

a window you close is forgotten so an agent's show lands in the window you used before it, a show can name its window, the desktop app raises the window a show lands on, and two windows refreshing at once spend one login token between them (#2341)
after a restart the listing resync answers from the last completed pass instead of queueing behind a running one, and a cold server builds one shared pass for all waiting clients (#2313)

auto-switch now restarts a session frozen on a usage limit within one 15 second tick of the pointer moving, instead of minutes later: the 120 second quiet check counts the age of Claude's own limit-stop record, not just the tmux repaint of its countdown screen (#2365)

carnivore now lives in the dock: closing the window leaves it running, the window comes back where you left it, cmd-q quits the app only with a one-time notice, quit and stop engine is its own item, a login launch opens no window unless you ask for one, and the menu bar icon can be turned off in settings (#2310)

carnivore:// links open a session, project, approvals popup or settings page in the desktop app (navigation only, anything malformed is refused), and the global hotkey brings the app forward or opens the session waiting on you longest, with a registration failure shown in settings (#2315)

in the desktop app every same-origin pop-out opens as its own native window with its own renderer (a plain browser keeps the new tab), the open windows are listed in the Window menu and come back after a restart, and the shell gains the window host and three digits-only window channels (#2330)

in the desktop app every window gets native Mac tabs (merge and split from the Window menu, one tab group per window kind), system full screen, and a hidden-inset title bar whose traffic lights no control sits under, with the top strip as the window's drag region (a browser tab shows none of it) (#2338)

logging into a codex account from a phone, another computer on the network or a paired computer now uses codex's device code login (a code and a link you open anywhere) instead of a localhost callback that could never finish

mcphealth is catalog only: the compiled-in plugin left the binary, an install that had it on keeps its settings, reads needs_approval until the owner approves the catalog sheet, loses the stale built-in ledger row and gets one alert pointing at warez

one shared process table snapshot (no older than one two-second cycle) serves the attention watcher's early passes, the mcp health monitor and the session journal, so ps runs about once per cycle instead of once per triggered pass (#2314)
opening a session asks the server for exactly the 5000 rows the terminal keeps, not its 10000-line default, so the older half is no longer transferred and parsed only to be trimmed (#2384)

opening the dashboard over a session and pressing Escape no longer leaves the session's grid empty, so tabs open again: the terminal grid is not torn down and rebuilt while the dashboard lies over the main area (#2359)

quitting carnivore with cmd-q now leaves the engine running: your agents, phone alerts and the server log keep going, the next launch picks the engine up without a click, an engine from another version gets one restart-or-quit dialog, and quit and stop engine (or an update install) stops it through its own shutdown route (#2320)
reading one Task Manager item no longer re-selects and re-sorts the whole list to number it: a list's number map is kept until the next database commit

redeploying the AWS gate runner at a new commit now runs the dependency prep build itself when that commit has none staged, so the clean room (gate 11) no longer fails its install and reports gate_missing (#2367)
restarting a session that an open layout holds now happens in place: the layout stays on screen with every tile instead of dropping to that one session full screen (#2371)

returning to a running session opens the terminal socket at once and fetches the saved history beside it; live output is held (64 KiB, oldest shed and announced) until the history is written, so history is always first and never lands under a live byte (#2346)

review fixes for the Dock app: a minimized pop-out no longer pins the terminal size, a viewer cut off by overflow gets no stale output before its resync marker, a venv built by an unsupported Python is rebuilt, and a reload or cached page no longer leaves the show target missing

review fixes for the Dock app: open in editor and a custom terminal command run only after you click Run on a native dialog showing the exact command, the app window and its bridge use the loopback address only, the app refuses to adopt an engine port held by another user, banner buttons only open the app while the screen is locked, the global hotkey refuses chords like Cmd+C and Cmd+Shift+Q, and the terminal command settings can no longer be written by an agent

changes.details: hosted/catalog_index/seed_tree.py builds the one-commit seed of the slim public catalog repo (item folders, README, marketplace file) from the old repo and fills the private metadata store; resign_plan.py writes the re-sign sitting's plan for the current releases. Nothing live changes. Issue 2373, epic 2063.
changes.summary: seed tree and re-sign plan tooling for the catalog slim plan

signing in with the authenticator code on a fresh page now leaves the login form (it used to stay up behind the app, so a second tap re-sent the spent code); a reused code says 'that code was just used. wait for the next one.' instead of [object Object] (#2350)

changes.details: The gate and review buildspecs build the catalog view (slim public repo plus private metadata plus the app's control plane) instead of cloning the catalog for its tools; the gate and review roles gain read on the metadata bucket; batch_review and batch_from_dir fall back to the app's hosted/catalog_index/tools. Nothing live changes until the runner is redeployed. Issue 2373, epic 2063.
changes.summary: submission gate and AI review build the catalog view instead of cloning the catalog for tools

terminals turn on xterm screen reader mode when the computer reports a screen reader (or when a setting forces it), the page language follows the locale, and the sessions list and notice dismiss are named from the string catalog (#2398)

the app bundle now carries a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES file and Chromium's license page, generated at build time from the payload lock, the pinned python and tmux builds, each wheel's own license metadata, Electron and the app's npm packages; a locked wheel or payload binary with no license name and text stops the build

the app checks a downloaded update before restarting into it: it must be signed by the Carnivore team and be a strictly newer version (semver, prerelease aware), otherwise the update is refused and nothing is stopped
the app now has a full mac menu bar with file, session, window and help menus, and option as meta works in every open terminal as soon as you switch it on (#2323)

the automations page opens simple: an overview of tiles and cards, a review feed of runs with a quick-view drawer, and a three-way schedule field (words, pick, cron); every older feature is kept under the advanced tab
the desktop app has a settings page for approval banners and the macOS notification permission, the global hotkey, login items, the menu bar icon, option as meta and the terminal app (#2303)

the desktop app settings page shows the address the server listens on and whether the connection is encrypted; the loopback default for new installs is deferred because Pack and federation TLS joins depend on the bind (#2306)

the desktop app shows a macOS banner for every open agent dialog (permission, codex approval, plan, folder trust, questions) with the dialog's own options as buttons, and a press answers it with no window open (#2307)
the dock icon now shows a red count of sessions waiting on you, its menu offers new session, recent projects and the waiting sessions, and it hops once when a new question arrives (#2318)
the elite file area labels a cplug row CPL instead of logging a missing translation key

the engine payload (python and tmux with their libraries) is signed inside out with the Developer ID, hardened runtime and a secure timestamp, python and tmux carry zero entitlements, and the bundle gains payload-manifest.json listing every third-party binary with its upstream URL, version and sha256

the feature catalog now describes the Dock app with its optional menu bar icon, and has entries for the Dock app, open in a terminal app with the Finder drop, export diagnostics and the faster terminal open; every native entry says why no capture shows it (#2354)

changes.details: pytest.ini norecursedirs now skips hosted/catalog_index/tools/tests, which has its own tests package and runs in a subprocess from tests/catalog_index/test_index_builder_suite.py. Collected in-process it killed the whole suite with ImportPathMismatchError. Issue 2373.
changes.summary: the full test suite collects again: the moved index builder suite is left to its own subprocess test
the home analytics panel now shows tokens per agent: a line per agent over 1h, 24h or 1w, with the running agents and their tokens per minute below

the home dashboard opened from a terminal page now lies over the main area only, so the session drawers and rails stay visible; a dashboard opened from the dashboards page shows there too instead of a new window; Escape returns to the view you came from (#2359)
the huddle held tell reaches the one-shot quiet-refusals flag through the sdk door session_bring_up instead of importing core, so it obeys the plugin import boundary

the link icon before a remote computer in the drawer's pack section and in settings now goes grey within about half a minute of that computer going quiet (a restart or an update), instead of staying green until the next slow refresh (#2362)

the mac app is hardened: electron fuses close run-as-node, node options and inspect and check the app's own asar, the release script reads the built binary's fuses and refuses a mismatch, a second launch brings the first window forward instead of starting another copy, the bridge refuses sub-frames, and the server folder is private to you (#2297)

the mac build is one universal app (apple silicon and intel) with a macos 14 floor, electron 44.7.0 and its build tools pinned to exact versions, and the release script refuses a range, a mismatched install, an arm64-only target or a newer eligible electron (#2295)

the off-by-default control-mode keystroke path no longer replays unconfirmed keys into another tmux server's pane after a server crash, finishes only its own writes during recovery, follows the session's active pane on every write, and leaves nothing queued when it cannot tell what landed

the payload signing check no longer fails open: --verify-app reads entitlements with a form that errors loudly, checks team, hardened runtime and timestamp per file, covers fat executables, verifies the app the run built, and a release refuses CARNIVORE_SKIP_PAYLOAD=1
the phone link and peer listeners no longer let uvicorn install its own unredacted log handler over the redacting route, and the log hygiene test no longer inherits that state from other tests
the release build can now produce a self-contained engine runtime (pinned Python and tmux, hashed lock) for both Mac architectures and place it in the app bundle; nothing runs it yet

the release build re-stamps latest-mac.yml and drops the stale dmg blockmap after the dmg is stapled, so the manifest matches the final bytes and the publish script verifies without a hand-corrected copy

the review lock: an agent cannot set a task to review while one of its subtasks is not in review or done, and your tick is refused while a subtask is not done or the task still waits on a blocker; the tick says why by subtask title or blocker instead of closing, and the agent guide explains subtasks, the lock and how to clear each blocker (guide rev 109)

the sidebar's two top rows have breathing room: the logo bar's menu, plus, bell and panel keys sit a step apart, and the counts strip has space at its edges and between the counts, the token rate and the chart (#2337)

the style guide no longer reaches /app-update while it runs signed out; the v41 schema step keeps the text it shipped with (the v97 step widens the consent check) and the v97 rung has its ledger line; the runner install lock follows the dependency floors
the terminal page and the home dashboard no longer share one measured box, so opening the dashboard over a session and pressing Escape leaves the session's grid and tabs in place (#2359)

the third-party notices file now also covers the browser-side code: every package vite bundles into the web build (read from its own module lists), the libraries vendored under client/vendor (xterm and its add-ons, CodeMirror and its packages) and the fonts, each with its license text; a bundled package, vendored file or font folder with no license stops the build
the tokens per agent chart now shows the newest minute and follows new usage by itself, no longer drops to zero at its right edge, wraps its legend instead of paging it, and drops the stray unit word
the top-down gate refuses a new hand-written button or field outside the base layer, with a per-file baseline that only goes down (#2361)

the update check now looks at the same app the installer would pick from a downloaded update (one real top-level app, the right bundle id, the full signing requirement, a release build), the stable feed refuses prerelease versions, and the update-proof marker is read only by proof builds

the update proof can run again: a build stamped as an update-proof build (signed into the app) may use a loopback update feed and install another update-proof build, while a release build still refuses any feed but the two official ones

the warez gate 10 AI review now hands the reviewer absolute folder paths, so it no longer answers review unavailable in the AWS runner, and a failed review records the reviewer's exit code and a scanned stderr tail in the job log (#2364)
the warez publish code lock is open (publish_pr.PUBLISH_ENABLED True); the env PUBLISH_ENABLED set to exactly 1 on the runner is the one control, and the first approved row is the canary

the widget settings overlay, the widget info popover, the duplicate widget prompt and the components list wear the base buttons (a little more compact), with their spacing and tracking from tokens (item 1192, chrome)
typing a trailing semicolon through the keystroke fallback no longer loses it: tmux read it as a command separator, so 'trail;' arrived as 'trail'

with auto update off, an available update turns the menu bar icon red with a white up arrow, puts a one-click update row first in the menu, posts one Notification Center notice with an update button, and opens a window that shows the download, check, install and restart (#2368)

you can open any local session in your own terminal app (ghostty, iterm2, terminal, kitty, wezterm or a command you confirm) from the session menu, the terminal widget menu and the menu bar rows (#2328)
