a Mac without the developer tools no longer shows Apple's install dialog from the secret scan, project worktrees, the server status commit line, the project pack git check or the agent exclude lookup, and a slow developer-tools lookup no longer holds up every other git check

a Mac without the developer tools no longer shows Apple's install dialog while Carnivore runs: one guard finds out whether git is installed without running it, the engine's boot, update check, rule history and git status reads skip git when it is absent, and installing the tools later turns those features on within seconds

a banner reply typed into a notification that launched the app cold now only opens the approval, because the app cannot tell a locked screen at launch; the 90 second engine wait is real time; a reply with a control character is refused with a visible notice instead of a silent failure
a browser that reaches this computer by its short hostname is no longer refused
a cplug whose code the ai review could not fully see is now blocked, and its manifest and python files are shown to the reviewer first
a cplug's bare id can no longer be held by two handles, and a cplug blocked by the ai review cannot be sent back through the gates over the same files

a crafted archive from a paired computer can no longer write a file outside the target folder: the receiver refuses any file that would pass through a link and any link that is absolute or holds a parent step, and a project remote that embeds a login is never sent or used

a credential-shaped string in a gate report no longer erases a blocked ai review: the fail verdict is kept (text dropped) so a cplug or mod row ends as failed instead of being rolled again until clean
a definitive ai review block on a cplug or mod now stays blocked even when another gate in the same run came back undetermined, and an admin regate can no longer reset a row a block just landed on

a first publish for a new handle no longer crashes the runner when the store has no curator record: the new publisher record takes the release key, and a setup fault releases the rows with its real reason

a fresh desktop install no longer reloads its window into an engine that is about to restart for the rebind, which left the sign-in gate painted with raw keys; the reload now waits until the engine answers again
a move no longer waits forever on an agent whose only open work is a background shell

a move now sees a resting agent's open background shells and stops them itself instead of waiting until it gives up: the move read its row without the open shell count the sidebar shows, so it never knew only shells held the turn end; the transfer toast also says plainly that a running turn is waited out, never stopped

a nuke run from a checkout no longer stops the live engine by name, nor deletes the app's shared per-user folders, state directory or login jobs; only the app's own copy of the script (or a redirected home) owns them; the uninstall script's app-process pattern is anchored so a process that only names an app path is not killed

a pack transfer (send an agent, move a project or company) now shows a persistent status card in the bottom right corner with what is moving, where, the step, the elapsed time and a cancel that stops it before its point of no return; the send dialog hands the transfer to the card instead of leaving it running unseen, a second send points at the running one, finished and failed transfers stay until dismissed, and a transfer left unfinished by an app restart is closed instead of haunting the list; a refused turn end names its real blocker; and a move of a resting agent that only has open background shells stops those shells itself (the send dialog says so first, the card shows 'stopping 2 background shells'), while a copy or a new agent there never stops them

a packaged app no longer asks the private development repository for release tags through git: with no .git in its server folder the tag check is not applicable and the version route reports null instead of an answer, and the peer toolchain report no longer counts Apple's git and python3 stubs as installed tools
a publish no longer aborts at the marketplace step after signing: the generator now gets an absolute catalog path instead of one resolved a second time from inside its tools folder
a revocation waiting for the publish bot is measured from the moment it was revoked, so the oldest waiting time no longer reads millions of minutes and the publish queue alarm stays quiet
a revoke run now pushes a marketplace-only commit to the public catalog main so the index build no longer fails its marketplace check and the revocation reaches the signed index
a second refresh press inside the ten second floor now still stops a revoked third-party sidecar, and a credential-shaped gate report keeps its fail gate ids
a session moved to a paired computer keeps showing under its original project on the computer it left, instead of a second project named with a (2) suffix
a session you moved to a paired computer shows up in this computer's list again: the stopped row a move leaves behind no longer hides the paired computer's row for the same session

after an app restart while the screen is locked, a banner button press only opens the app until the owner unlocks: the lock tracker now starts locked and reads macOS's own lock flag at launch, instead of assuming unlocked

an Intel Mac can install and build the app again: cryptography is pinned to 48.0.1 on Intel and 50.0.0 on Apple silicon, because 49 and later publish no Intel macOS wheel, and a test now checks every locked package has a wheel for each architecture the release ships

desktop banners got an inline reply field for questions that take only typed text (2000 character cap, sent to the dialog answer route), one Notification Center thread per session, a notification id per banner, a pinned action-index argument for Electron 45, and a typed reply that launched the app is answered after the engine is up

engine login service review fixes (off by default): a login item turned on later is no longer removed at launch, the service stops respawning an engine that keeps dying, a leftover service is honored by a window that reads the detached default, dropped folders and links reach the window the service opens, and a failed login bookkeeping write never blocks the engine start

every tmux call the server makes now uses the binary that matches the live tmux server, not only the session backend, and the menu bar terminal and offline session count pick the same binary the server does, so a bundled newer tmux never drives an older live server
move the pack in-flight tracker and op status modules into core/pack/move/ so only __init__ sits flat under core/pack

moving a project or company now starts its agents on the other computer for you: the ones that were running here are woken there once the move succeeds, the status card says how many started and names any that did not with the reason, and agents that were already asleep stay asleep

moving a whole project or company no longer refuses while agents are running: the plan lists them ('2 agents will stop here and continue on studio', plus how many background shells will be stopped) and the move itself waits for every agent's turn to end, stops resting agents' open background shells, puts them to sleep and then transfers, with the status card showing each step; a turn that never ends fails with the agent's real blocker and nothing is stopped, and a cancel wakes the agents again

moving a whole project whose folder is not a git repo but holds repos now sends each repo with its history and uncommitted work, plus the loose files, instead of one archive, when the other computer is new enough; older computers still get the archive

nuke, stop and reset find the server by the process LISTENING on its port, never by every process connected to it; nuke stops a listener only when it is in this install's own process identity (its dev Electron, or a src.main running from its folder) and says so when it leaves another one alone

publishing is now a page of the warez store instead of a window: your submissions with four stages (submitted, in review, approved, rejected), a dossier for each item with its next step, the 12 checks, a timeline built from real times, a card image step, the send limits and the rules, and withdraw and appeal from the page
quitting the app with Cmd-Q now exits it: the second quit is issued after the first one has returned, so the app no longer closes its window and lingers in the tray and Dock

retiring the old python environment now also clears its install marker so a later boot rebuilds it properly, only an engine the app itself started counts toward the three healthy launches, a read-only settings folder no longer stops the app starting, and the launch-at-login record follows the owner's latest choice until the new login service has carried it

review fixes for the engine login service: only an explicit detached setting unregisters it (a typo or unreadable file keeps it, and a switch-back clears carriedBy), and a window whose adopted service engine went quiet re-adopts it once it answers again (#2440, #2442)
revoking a version from the first party script now pushes the regenerated marketplace file in the same step, or refuses to finish and names the exact command, so the next index build no longer fails
revoking a version now builds its catalog view fresh from the store, and a regenerated marketplace file that would drop or change an unrelated live entry is refused before anything is pushed

sending an agent now carries the project's memory folder the first time the project reaches a computer, keeps the longer copy of a conversation that ran under a relay profile, and tells the agent where it is now with a note in its memory folder (an interrupted agent also gets the folder map after continue)

sending an agent now refuses, with a plain sentence and before anything sleeps, when its folder holds work the other computer cannot take (nested repos, worktrees outside the folder, loose files), carries the project's commits before the move starts, and fails the move when that carry fails instead of landing the agent in an empty folder

sending an agent to a computer on the new version now also carries its git worktrees that live outside the project folder (branch, commits and uncommitted work), puts them at the same place under the other computer's home when that is free, and tells the agent where each folder landed in its memory note

sending an agent to a computer on the new version now carries its nested repos, its uncommitted work (staged, unstaged and untracked files, byte for byte) and the loose files of its folder before the move starts, and refuses without writing anything when the other computer has changes of its own in the way

stop.sh and reset.sh stop a port listener only when it is a src.main running from their own checkout (one shared helper with nuke.sh), the shell port resolver follows the server's order (process environment, last .env assignment with export and quotes, default), and the nuke sandbox environment cannot reach the real app

switching the engine host from detached back to launchd-agent registers the engine login service again even when no LaunchAgent plist exists, while a login item turned off in System Settings is still not re-registered by a relaunch, and a service facing a port holder it cannot replace logs the mismatch once per holder and retries the replace once a minute instead of logging every tick forever

the Mac app now boots its engine on the bundled python and tmux payload when the app carries one for this computer, with the payload bin first on PATH and no Homebrew, venv or pip needed; a build or install with no payload (a dev checkout, the local install) keeps starting the engine the old way
the agents and shells counts no longer show in the terminal status bar by default; turn either on in settings, appearance, status bar, and it shows

the ai review of a cplug can no longer be steered by the author: the server's kind picks the reviewer, a cplug may not carry another kind's manifest or any image, and its manifest version must match the version being published

the app window no longer goes blank after the first-run engine restart: the window reload that was held back for the restart now waits until the new engine answers health instead of firing the moment it is spawned
the archive toggle on the Projects page now also shows archived agent sessions under their projects, without needing show-hidden or the closed toggle

the default Home layout (fresh install, new device, reset to default) is now the stat strip, token history with estimated cost, tokens by project, model and agent, running sessions beside the provider ledger, then recently closed sessions, skills and plugins; a saved Home layout is untouched

the desktop app can post a macOS notification only for toasts that ask you something (asks only, off by default), and settings explain Focus allowed apps with a button that opens the Focus pane (#2459)

the desktop app can run the engine as a headless login service (off by default, the detached engine stays the default): it starts at login with no window, restarts itself when the app is updated, sends every Dock click to a real window that adopts it, and a first-run engine is adopted by loopback health before any port test

the desktop app moves to electron 45.0.0, and the release script now requires the pin to be the newest stable electron on npm with no two-week wait and no override, so an electron update ships as a security update at once
the desktop app plan document now states the Electron pin rule as it is: the newest stable at once, no two-week wait

the engine login service follows the owner's switch: reading detached again unregisters it, a SIGTERM to a window no longer waits behind the first-quit notice, and a window that adopted the service's engine stays down when the service is quit on purpose instead of starting its own (#2440, #2441, #2442)

the engine login service no longer stops a same-version engine that replaced the one it adopted: teardown now also requires the same listener process id, and the refusal log line no longer claims no server is running when another engine answers on the port

the engine login service no longer stops an engine of another version that holds its port: it logs once, waits and asks again about once a minute, and the window's take-over dialog is where the owner decides

the engine login service no longer stops or restarts an engine it adopted once a different version has replaced it on the port: it drops the adoption, logs it, and waits for the owner's take-over decision like any other foreign holder

the engine login service's first-run rebind no longer stops a same-version engine that replaced the one it adopted: the rebind restart takes the same stop gate (same version, same listener process id) as teardown
the engine service no longer exits and stays down when another user's program holds the engine port: it logs once and asks again about once a minute, as the docs say

the engine service no longer sends a sign-in code to a program on the engine port that is not yours, the service launches one window per burst of dropped folders or links, and tray Nuke logs under your own temp folder and runs without a shell (#2445, #2446, #2447, #2448)

the engine service no longer shuts down a replacement engine that reports no version when it tears down or restarts for an update, and the quit log says no server is running instead of claiming an adopted one was refused
the engine service no longer stops an engine it did not start or adopt when it restarts for a new bundle or is told to quit; it leaves that engine for the take-over dialog and logs it (#2454)

the engine service now treats a different process holding the engine port as a new holder: it logs the mismatch and replaces it at once instead of waiting up to a minute behind the previous holder's backoff; the payload doc now says the launch at login record is refreshed until the login service carries it

the engine service review notes are closed: an unknown engine host setting is logged capped and quoted, a clock stepped back no longer holds the restart bounds spent, a window restarts the login service for an older engine only when the listener is provably this user's own and at most once per version per 30 minutes, a staged tmux copy is reused only when its bytes still match its hash, and raise, focus and tear-off requests from one window are limited to one per 500 ms
the engine-already-running dialog now raises the app before it opens, so it is not hidden and Cmd-Q is no longer ignored behind it
the first Add in the add-folder alert no longer fails when the alert sat open for a few seconds: a request that hits a connection the server already closed is sent once more on a fresh one
the hosted theme validator accepts the --legacy-radius-sm, -md and -lg tokens the app theme contract gained in #2260, so theme uploads that carry them are no longer refused
the index build says a folder left on main belongs to a revoked release instead of suggesting a lost publish
the installer's download address is now checked against the release architecture file at site deploy, and its Intel swap no longer doubles the universal suffix once the pin names the universal build

the launch lock read now treats any console-session shape it does not fully understand (a nested dict, a flag that is not a plain true or false, disagreeing entries, unbalanced tags) as unknown and stays locked, instead of reading it as unlocked

the login service's once-per-version restart bound now holds per version and ignores a version that is not a short string, the bundled tmux is hashed once per launch, the engine port-holder message names the listener and not a connected client, and the intel installer tells a missing build apart from a failed download check
the login service's restart bounds now count a version reported as the string __proto__ like any other version, so it can no longer bypass the once-per-version limit

the one-command installer picks the universal download on an Intel Mac and stops with a clear message while none is published, the payload app no longer deletes a cloudflared it did not verify, and a very slow first boot still counts toward retiring the old python environment

the pack section's computers are on/off switches: click one to hide every agent and project running on that computer from the sidebar, click again to show them; every computer starts on and the choice is kept per device class
the pairing reload is also held while the rebind restart is already running, so a health probe landing as the old engine shuts down no longer reloads the window into it

the payload build keeps the user's Homebrew tools on every session's PATH, no longer puts its own python ahead of theirs, keeps its tmux settings out of the sessions, keeps a stable copy of its tmux so a running server survives an app update, and Reinstall Server Environment no longer breaks the engine

the per-window request bound now also covers opening a session window and showing a row in the main window, the 500 ms gate stays open when the clock steps back, and the engine only runs a staged tmux copy whose folder name is the hash of its bytes

the pinned left rail marks the open page's key (war room and every other menu page), as the expanded menu already did; the war room page loses its top title line and its widget strip wears the same icon as its menu row

the publish flow can send a sidecar plugin (cplug): it lists the folders you sideloaded, checks the author contract before upload (id grammar, runtime, data, network hosts), and prepares a copy with your publisher id, catalog tier and default off

the runner dependency lock follows the cryptography 50.0.0 bump, a publish setup fault now lists the rows it released and keeps each earlier drop's own reason, and the warez docs describe the direct push to main
the runner's alert for changes to its CodeBuild projects now matches the project ARN that CloudTrail records, so an UpdateProject on a carnivore-runner project raises the alert
the runner's publish step no longer imports boto3 against the locked botocore (the first canary publish died on it), and a crashed runner command now fails its build instead of passing as a verdict

the runner's publish step now sees each author's handle state (the listing hid it, so every approved row was dropped as unconfirmed), and a row dropped before staging says why in its release reason and in the publish output
the send dialog now shows a plain checklist before you confirm: what comes along, what stays behind and why, tools the agent ran that the other computer may lack, and servers that will stop

the send dialog's move and the project move have a box, off by default, to stop running agents now and continue them on the other computer: with it off a move refuses up front and names every agent that is mid-turn, with it on each running agent gets an interrupt, the move runs, the agents wake on the other computer and only the interrupted ones are told to continue; also, background shells are now stopped only after the agent is asleep (so the agent cannot react to the exit with a new turn), and an agent at its prompt with only background shells open no longer counts as running

the store front door now takes plugins that run as sandboxed sidecars (kind cplug) from community authors: the hosted validator checks the folder against the same rules as the app's install gate, and the macOS clean-room test is dropped by decision

the store's gates and the catalog index now accept third-party sidecar plugins (cplugs): the static gates and the AI review still run, the macOS clean room is recorded as skipped by policy, and the index no longer refuses a community cplug

the update progress window and the server-down status window paint in the packaged app again: with the hardened file-protocol fuse off, a page loaded from inside app.asar over file:// is not found, so each window now serves its own page from its own session on a private page scheme

the warez page's refresh now stops a revoked running plugin at once instead of within the hour, the app refuses a plugin folder carrying another kind's manifest before upload, and the schema set pin matches the open cplug policy again so the index job passes

uninstall and nuke now agree: both unregister the engine login service and remove both LaunchAgent labels, reset our privacy rows, keep your projects folder, and end terminal sessions only when you ask (--stop-tmux); nuke.sh runs from a packaged install and finds the app's own python

uninstall and nuke review fixes: nuke stops this install's own app and server by identity (agents in your sessions keep running), nuke never deletes a projects folder or your home through a configured folder, the login service is found and unregistered wherever the app is, and the system steps (app, tccutil) run only for the packaged app's nuke

upgrading from 1.16 keeps your pairing, settings and data in place; launch at login is recorded and kept until the new login service exists; the old python environment is removed only after the built-in engine started cleanly on three launches; the built-in engine no longer downloads cloudflared on first run

Start Server no longer refuses for about 30 seconds after another user's server on the port dies: with nothing listening and no health answer it waits up to 45 seconds for the port to free up, then starts; the login-off click now records launch at login as off at once; the login service logs one plain line naming the port when it leaves a holder that is not ours alone

While Start Server waits for a stale port to free up, a second click starts nothing, the tray stays on starting and shows "waiting for port 8000 to free up", and a port held by a non-Carnivore process makes the login service wait and retry instead of counting a failed start

a Carnivore plugin published under plugins/ also carries a byte-identical cplugs/ copy at its signed commit, deleted again in the marketplace commit, and the index builder refuses a plugins/ version without it, so apps 1.16.2 and 1.16.3 keep installing every plugin
a Carnivore plugin's install folder comes from the signed source path (plugins/ or legacy cplugs/)
a new install opens both widget bars pinned open: the bottom bar with the terminal and scheduled tasks, the right bar with files, notes and bookmarks; an existing arrangement is never changed
a new terminal from the plus menu opens with no error: the console no longer shows the 'that folder holds other projects' message for the home folder it always starts in
a plugin published with no image of its own now gets a generated hero at publish, Carnivore plugins included

a plugin view in the widget drawer shows the plugin's own description instead of a raw text key, is listed under a plugins heading as a plugin view, and the test server reset can delete the read-only plugin runtime files

a plugin view that is shown as a widget can declare which sizes it supports and its smallest size in its cplug.json (fits), so the cell menu size gear and resizing offer exactly those; a view that declares none keeps medium, large and full
a plugin you approve that runs with no sandbox can now ship its own panel view files (html, css, js, svg, png, woff2) in a catalog install; every other plugin keeps the old file list

a script stages the catalog move of Carnivore plugins from cplugs/ to plugins/ in a fresh clone, checks the built index items against the live index, runs the field install gate and prints the push command only while the commit is still a fast-forward of the catalog main
a third-party plugin can ship one preview image, shown as its widget drawer thumbnail and on its plugins page card

a third-party plugin you approve can ask to run with no sandbox (trust unrestricted in its manifest) so it can reach your network and files; only a release signed by the app's publisher key, or a local plugin you consented to, ever runs that way, and the permission sheet says it has full access to this computer

after carnivore refuses to start because another program holds the port, a carnivore link, a folder drop or a second launch no longer opens a window onto that program's page, and a page toast with banners off no longer asks macos for notification permission

an app window that is already open stops sending its sign-in and API calls to whatever answers on the engine port after an outage until the same holder check as the start path passes; another user's program on the port keeps the block and the tray shows the existing refusal, and the window recovers by itself when the engine is ours again (#2494)

an installed download plugin can be uninstalled from its own panel, even after the store pulled its listing: the panel shows uninstall for any plugin with a catalog ledger row, with the same confirm sheet as the warez detail
an update that stops the engine and then cannot start the install now starts the engine again and offers try again, instead of leaving the engine stopped

an update the system refuses to install after the restart request no longer leaves the app half stopped: the engine is started again, the progress window shows the failure with a working try again, and the update log names the error

clicking Start Server in the menu bar menu opens the app window once the engine answers when no window is open, through the same path as a Dock click; the login service, launch, supervisor restart and update relaunch never open one
compaction points no longer appear in the bookmarks widget or panel; they are not bookmarks, and every bookmark a person made stays

macos no longer asks for notification permission when the app starts with approval banners off; the first request happens when you turn banners on, and until you answer it the desktop settings say where the prompt is, at the top right of the screen
on a first launch the window now waits up to three seconds for the engine's setup to settle, so the one rebind restart runs before the window opens instead of two seconds under it

on a fresh install's first launch the sign-in window now opens after the one-time engine restart instead of under it, so it shows the themed sign-in page once, with no gray unthemed gate and no reload
plugin messages, docs and catalog text now call every plugin a plugin
publishing a plugin is one choice: Claude Code plugins and Carnivore plugins list under a single plugin button in the publish dialog
shift-click on a terminal tab's close control now kills the session and closes the tab in one go on a layout page too, instead of leaving a session ended tab to close again

the 1.0 gate gains a field installs stage that runs every app version from 1.16.2 up against each plugin in the live catalog index, so a release that breaks an older plugin is caught before a version bump

the app's bundled python no longer writes bytecode into the signed app, so a deep codesign verify stays clean after the engine has run: every payload python start (the engine under any host, the offline session list, the diagnostics fallback, the MCP bridge) keeps its .pyc files in ~/Library/Caches/Carnivore/pycache, or writes none when that folder cannot be made
the catalog admin queue has four tabs, submitted, in review, approved and rejected, each with a count, and every row shows one plain status word instead of thirteen tabs and raw gate states

the catalog now refuses a plugin the app would refuse to install before it signs it: the publish page checks carnivore.json against the app's own schema, and the local publish step runs the app's install gates on every plugin it stages
the catalog publish and index checks now accept panel view files for an approved unrestricted plugin, the same rule the app install gate uses

the first launch no longer shows a blank window or raw sign-in keys after the app restarts its own engine (the reload now waits for the window guard to clear), and a tray Stop Server is no longer undone by the supervisor

the first launch opens the window only after the app has finished restarting its own engine onto the configured address, so there is no long empty window, and stopping that engine no longer logs a false 'another program holds the port' warning

the first window on a cold launch paints the sign-in page as soon as the engine answers: the window guard now holds the first load until its holder check passes instead of cancelling it, so the 20 second blank window and the two blocked-load errors are gone

the hosted catalog tooling reads Carnivore plugins from both plugins/ and the legacy cplugs/ folder, trusts each release's signed path, and writes new ones to plugins/, so the public catalog repo can move cplugs/ into plugins/ with the live index unchanged

the join helper, the carnivore command-line shim and the codex supervisor now keep the bundled python's bytecode out of the signed app too, and the payload build no longer leaves timestamp-based bytecode files that python would rewrite after packaging
the launch's venv-retire report moved out of the menu bar app's main file into the venv-retire module, no behavior change, so the main file is back under its size ceiling
the macos notification prompt no longer appears when carnivore launches with approval banners off, and the waiting note shows right after you turn banners on

the packaged app now tracks the screen lock for real, so an approval banner pressed on a locked screen only opens the app instead of answering; and the restart choice on the older-engine dialog at launch now has a signed client, so it can stop the older engine and start this version's
the plugins list tool for agents is now plugins_list and also lists plugins installed from the catalog; cplugs_list still answers
the plugins page draws the same card as warez, with its hero image, and lists store plugins in the same order
the plugins page lists every downloadable plugin, Claude Code and Carnivore alike; a Carnivore plugin's switch opens the install sheet
the plugins page shows warez's add control on a store plugin that is not installed and update when one is due, so only an installed plugin shows an on and off switch
the warez plugins tab lists every plugin, Claude Code plugins and Carnivore plugins together, with one count, one kind tag and one picture

the window guard now re-checks the engine port's holder on every healthy poll, so another user's program that takes the port with no failed poll is caught; the engine supervisor still restarts a dead engine during a guard refusal; a window whose load was cancelled while blocked reloads when the block lifts; and an error in the guard can no longer stop the health poll (#2494)

the window guard stays closed for a whole outage after a deliberate stop, a first window is not opened onto a program that took the port during the app's own restart, and a login-service or adopted engine is never restarted (or asked about) before the first window
the words shown while a start waits for a stale port to free up print the port as plain digits (8000) instead of 8,000
turning off start at login from an app that login started now removes the login item, instead of the app killing itself and leaving the item in place
turning off start-at-login from the app that login started now also removes the loaded login job when the app quits, so a crash cannot bring the app back until you log out
turning start at login off now records it at the click, and the login job is dropped even if the app is killed with kill -9 afterwards, so a crash no longer brings the app back until logout

uninstalling a plugin that has nothing left to purge frees its name, so a purged then uninstalled plugin no longer lingers as a removed card; a removed card now says removed; the warez sidebar installed plugins count is the plugins page's own list, sidecar plugins included

waking a sleeping session whose conversation never reached disk now offers to start fresh: the same row, name, pin and place in the sidebar get a new conversation in the same folder under the same login, instead of a toast and a stuck row
waking or restarting an imported session finds its conversation when the transcript lives under a managed login's projects folder, instead of refusing with no transcript found
when another program holds the engine's port and carnivore refuses to start, it no longer opens its window onto that program's page after you close the dialog

with approval banners off the app no longer mirrors page toasts to macOS, so nothing can raise the notification permission prompt before you turn banners on; the waiting for macos hint now goes away on its own ten minutes after the request
with approval banners off, the update-available notice no longer asks macos for notification permission

Quit and Stop Engine, the update install and the old-version restart now work on an engine whose first-run setup is not finished: the tray holds no token then, so the engine's own loopback listener is stopped after the same-user check, and the tray tooltip says cannot determine instead of a zero session count
a backup drive alert already raised by the old default drive now clears on its own once the drive check is off

a computer with no time machine backup disk set up no longer raises a cannot tell time machine alert, and one already open closes by itself on the next check; a stale backup and the access and unreadable cases still alert

a debug-level log no longer crashes the session listing probe (the startup gate ledger and three other modules log through structlog, and a test refuses keyword logging on a stdlib logger), a failed write to a live pane answers 502 instead of 404 no such session, and shutdown, notification-store and validation-error logs carry their cause

a fresh desktop install stays on this computer only until you finish setup yourself: the menu bar app no longer pairs it by itself, the setup screen opens as soon as the engine answers, and the app signs in only after you finish
a fresh install no longer raises a backup drive is not connected alert: the state-backup drive check runs only when CARNIVORE_BACKUP_VOLUME names a drive

a plugin that asks for no permissions and whose code changed now has an approve button on its permissions tab; the sideload answer's needs_approval matches the row, and its routes answer 409 needs_approval instead of held off
a plugin whose first image idea uses a banned word gets a new idea instead of shipping with no image
a session row's right-click menu always offers pin and unpin, whether or not the inline pin icon is shown
a time machine check plugin, off by default: the check core runs today, as a switch on the plugins page

after updating from 1.16.3 or older, the first 1.16.4 launch asks for the authenticator code once, because the app window now opens on this computer's own address (127.0.0.1) and its old sign-in does not carry over; later updates do not ask again
an item shows unread only while there is something unread to see: agent tasks are born read, the owner's tick clears the dot, reading the last card clears it, and stale dots are swept once at startup
bookmarks and the timeline work on long conversations up to 2 GB, not 512 MB

carnivore no longer reads time machine on its own: the check is now the time machine check plugin, off for everyone. If you use time machine and want the alert, switch the plugin on in the plugins page. Its alert names carnivore as the sender, sits under other when you filter alerts by sender, and reaches a phone or chat destination only if you tick plugin alerts in notification settings; an alert left open by the old check closes at the next start.

deleted components nothing mounts: the launchpad's project tree, running list, recent list and attribution card, the old hosts page screen with its peer panes, the old pack computers panel with its pack name field and the history crosstalk card, with their tests, styles and style guide entries

deleted the last launchpad orphans nothing imports: the agent family and wrapper pills, the project tree host, chrome, groups and node, the recent and running chromes, the attribution prompt logic and running-row, with their tests, styles and style guide entries
deleted the launchpad session rows and attention group, and the old pack join form, that only the first deletion had mounted, with their golden and source-text test cases

deploy-dmg.sh swaps the app's Contents in one atomic exchange, so the installed app is never without code mid-install, and reads the backup drive after the install, stopping with exit 5 and the fix (switch Carnivore off and on in Full Disk Access) when the read is refused

developer sideload you can reach: the switch takes a duration (1 h, 12 h, 24 h, 7 days or until turned off), the Plugins page loads a plugin from a folder or from git (https or ssh, hardened fetch) with re-sync and remove on each sideloaded row, and MCP plugin_sideload_add and plugin_sideload_remove wait for the owner and refuse while the switch is off; turning the switch on passes a danger confirm every time, a danger strip shows while it is on, the load form and a changed re-sync carry the warning line, and the MCP add tool carries the same warning

every read-only database open goes through one helper that encodes the path, so a folder or file name with # or % can no longer open a different file; ten private atomic file writers now share one helper that syncs the file and its folder and cleans up its temp file; the stats routes are documented and typed
fix the admin queue and users panels retrying a failed load in a loop, and load the queue one status at a time, which took the catalog api down
fix the catalog api crashing at startup after the publish check shipped, so the store answers again

leftovers from the screens pass: the dead project tree and family pill styles, the attribution prompt and decline routes nothing calls, the mutation scripts and manual harness pages that named deleted files, and the Task Manager rail tabs test now expects the bell and its count
plugin alerts can carry their own strings, a detail line and actions, and a plugin can resolve its own alert; no plugin uses it yet

plugin code nobody approved never runs: after a sideload re-sync (or a plugin update) brings new code, approving it on the Plugins page starts the new code, and restart, app start, the plugin switch, a first call and a crash restart all refuse it until then (restart answers 409 needs_approval)
quit and stop engine no longer says the engine is already stopped when it could not look: a failed port lookup counts as running, and the health check follows a moved port
quit and stop engine no longer says the engine is already stopped while it still runs: the stop uses the port the engine was adopted on and counts any listening socket there as running

stopping an adopted engine whose first-run setup is unfinished now signals only the exact process recorded at adoption (same pid, start time, executable, port and version, sole listener), never another listener of the same user
store vitest: three stale tests fixed (kind guard allow-list, add menu blocked reason tooltip, hero image fixture indexKind)
the Task Manager's drawer icon shows the same needs-you number as the Task Manager itself, so plain fyi messages on tasks being worked no longer badge it
the Warez page now builds as its own bundle for catalog.carnivore.ai, reading the signed index from the same host through a static data adapter, wearing the app's look and tokens

the admin queue now derives its stage from the publish page's one stageOf rule and adds only its two extras (superseded is approved, withdrawn is rejected), so the two surfaces cannot drift; no behavior change
the alert center's recheck and retry buttons call the right route again (they requested a doubled /api/v1 path and failed), and the moved-to-warez plugin alert now has a declared kind
the backup drive name in the engine's .env is matched without regard to letter case, as the engine's other settings are, so a lowercase carnivore_backup_volume line turns the drive check on
the backup drive value in the engine's .env is read literally, so a reference to another key can no longer pull that key's value into the drive path shown in alerts
the files widget's rail key shows a bubble with how many files changed, the same count as the changes widget, and a rail key setting turns it off

the public Warez page is now read only: no add, install, installed menu, publish, refresh, rating or sign in controls; its detail offers get carnivore, the copyable item id and the source repository link, and a footer line names the signed index serial, dates and signing key

the public Warez page logs no console errors any more (the page policy now allows inline style attributes and nothing else inline), and on a phone it no longer draws the top left back arrow that left the page blank

the running sessions widget no longer draws a dark block over its name and task column (its wrapper shared a class name with the base task wrapper), and a drawer copy has a compact or normal choice in the widget menu: compact shows the name alone, normal (the default) adds a small dim line with the folder and last activity

the server stops repeating the same cheap questions: the tmux server version is asked once per server instead of every 5 seconds, subagent and session-record folders are listed only when the folder changed, and the deep search settings are read from config.json only when the file changed
the session timeline is always vertical, time running down at every width and in every host, and scrolls when the box is short
the sign-in window no longer flashes blank once a few seconds after it opens on a fresh install, and the tray start server window opens after the one-time engine restart instead of under it
the state-backup drive check can be turned on by one line in the engine's own .env file, which survives reboots and app updates and needs no restart; the process environment still wins

the stats feed, the stats answers writer, the automations reads, the background indexer and read scopes reuse one sqlite connection per thread and file instead of opening one per call, about 150 fewer connects a minute
waking or restarting a stopped session puts it straight back in the live list under its project, no server restart needed

when a program that is not ours holds the engine port and the app's three fast restarts are used up, the app keeps asking about once a minute and starts our engine by itself once the port is free; it never stops the other program, and a deliberate stop, a quit or an explicit start cancels the retry

when the app keeps checking about once a minute because another program holds the engine port, the menu bar now shows a Stop Retrying row that cancels the retry, so the owner can tell it to stop trying
withdrawing a send also withdraws its pending hero image, so the image no longer waits in the review queue forever once the item is taken back

a crosstalk message the receiver answered no longer expires and notifies the sender: the receiver's reply counts as the read receipt for a held native message, and expiry skips anything its receiver already replied to

a long message pasted into an agent no longer sits unsent in its input box: the paste waits for the pane to go quiet, presses Enter, checks the pane changed, presses again up to three times, and reports a failed delivery instead of claiming it was delivered
a paired computer's sleeping agents now show in this computer's sidebar with that computer's marker, hidden only by the show sleeping toggle, and waking one runs on the computer that owns it
a permission prompt in a short pane, where claude drops the Esc to cancel line and wraps the question, now reads as a normal approval card with its buttons, so Beast Mode can answer it
a plugin's inbound webhook no longer spends its per-minute budget on a stale or replayed copy of a signed request, so replaying one captured request cannot lock the real sender out

a project agent's swarm chat no longer shows every card on its project board as an info entry carrying the card's whole text, so no agent reading its thread spends tokens on it; the board keeps the cards, the one-line card events stay, and a new swarm setting, card text in agent chats (off by default), brings the old entries back for whoever wants them
a restarted session streams its output again on tmux 3.8, which drops the output pipe when the agent exits: the restart now reattaches it in the same tmux call, so even the first line shows

a review board attachment is kept only when its extension is on an allow-list (images, text and code including html, svg, css and js, pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, and mp4, mov, webm, mp3 and wav media) and its bytes match it; executables, shell scripts and archives are refused with a 415 and a reason; web and code files are also scanned for credentials
a scheduled wake-up goes to the task's own session first
a scheduled wake-up reaches a parked task, scheduled tasks are not nudged, and a refused wake-up says so on the task
a scheduled wake-up says on the task which session it woke

a sent swarm chat message shows its attached pictures as thumbnails under the words (the saved path lines are hidden); a click opens the picture full size; the bytes come from a new authenticated route that serves only png, jpeg, gif and webp files inside the session's own upload folder

changes.details: A plugin's carnivore.json can ask for a page and push topics. The menu and the page are the plugin's one view drawn twice, linked by ui.share; a phone shows one at a time behind a menu | view switch. Plugins stay sandboxed.
changes.summary: a sideloaded plugin can have its own page: a rail key, a slide-out menu and a main-area view, with pushed updates

a sideloaded plugin can now read an agent flow chart run through a new flow.read permission and flow.run host methods (large runs come in parts), behind the owner's consent tick; the flow collector moved out of the flow plugin into core

a text file attached to a review board is scanned for credentials before it is stored; one that holds a key or token is refused and the answer names the file and the kind of credential, never the value

after a restart the save vault no longer rereads every conversation whose files were only touched (same bytes, new modified time): the follower keeps what it already proved identical in the vault folder, so the busy minutes after each boot drop to a walk of the disk and a stat per file; a proof is kept only for a file that has been quiet for five minutes (so a half-written last line is still saved once it settles), is dropped when the unit's newest saved point changes, and belongs to one vault location; a changed or new transcript is still saved on the next pass

ai agent runs with no permission prompts need the typed unattended phrase, audio and file uploads are refused at the size cap as they stream in, a pairing activates once, the unread flag only marks sessions the app knows, a stats clear that fails can be retried, and an upload folder ignores itself in git

an agent's numbered answer reads in its chat the way it reads in the terminal: items keep their numbers instead of all showing 1., and the indented sub-points under each item sit nested under it, two-digit items included; notes and skill pages draw lists the same way

an attachment can be removed from a review board (DELETE route or task_manager_board_attachment_remove): it leaves the board's list and the board keeps a removed entry with its name, size and dates so the history stays honest; the file itself stays on the task
an image chip on the swarm chat composer shows a small thumbnail made from the local file; clicking it opens the picture full size in the app modal, and the preview url is revoked when the chip goes
applying an incremental carried git bundle on a paired computer no longer prunes the refs earlier bundles created, so the next incremental bundle still has its base
approving a chat card with a note is one write, and a stale-revision refusal now retries once on the latest revision instead of failing every time

creating a session no longer reports an unexpected crash as a 400 validation error: a bug now answers 500, a failed tmux or spawn answers 502, and only a real bad request answers 400; the session errors share one typed root

changes.details: The project list, the project storage rows, the asleep rows, the paired-peer roster and the crosstalk session details were each re-read from carnivore.db on every call (about 14 connects a second at idle). They now share the change cache and re-read only after the database commits. The change cache also forgets a file's entries when its watcher is reopened, so a restored database file is never answered from the old file. Issue 1180, slice 5c.
changes.summary: hot carnivore.db reads open the file once per commit instead of once per call, and a replaced database file is never served stale
review plugin code and AI findings in admin before deciding publication, with larger supported bundles
setup checks for claude code and says how to get it; the installer needs macos 14
the approval card for promoting project leads names each running session that will be stopped and resumed, instead of a generic warning
the bottom row of home widgets can be made taller: drag the grip under the last row downward and the home screen scrolls, drag it back up to shrink it to the window fit
the carnivore.ai website source moved to its own private repo (carnivore-site); the app repo keeps only uninstall.sh, the canonical uninstall script
the first automatic project lead pick is stored by the scheduler's boot step and before a due tell, no longer by a session listing or a roles GET

the live lineage pass reads only the bytes a running conversation appended since the last pass instead of the whole transcript, and starts over for a file that shrank or was rewritten; the milestones it records are unchanged

the login page reads the clipboard for a six digit code and, when it finds one, types it in and tries it for you; a wrong code shows no error and leaves the box empty, and each copied code is tried only once

the pack transfer card now draws a progress bar from the finished steps plus the real bytes sent in the step in flight, shows the size sent and an 'about Xm left' once a rate is measured, and has a details toggle that opens a bounded log of steps, sizes, the other computer's acknowledgements and errors; a step that moves no bytes shows the step bar alone, and the project 'sending the code' line no longer shadows the agent send's commits line

the remote host, respawn and listing cache tests run in a fresh worktree (an empty throwaway config.json when the checkout has none) and on tmux 3.8 (measured command numbers, an empty dead-pane pid, the transport's argv seam)

the save vault's follower costs far less while a big conversation is being written: after a one-line append to a conversation with about 2,500 sidecar files it now stats each file once instead of five times, no longer walks and symlink-checks every file, no longer probes every chunk or reads the whole saved-point list five times, and keeps each folder's listing and each transcript's working folder until they change; every new, changed and appended byte is still saved, a chunk the retention pass removes is never believed present, and a chunk deleted by hand is noticed again within ten minutes (measured on a copy of a real conversation: 13,200 stats and 2,500 symlink checks per pass down to 2,750 stats, about 200 ms of CPU down to about 50 ms)

the send dialog says once, at the top, whether the agent can go to that computer and, if not, why and the one fix (update it); ignored folders collapse into one quiet line instead of dozens of yellow rows, and refused options give one short gray reason
the send dialog's comes along list is just names plus one about-size line for what the send carries; the sub-labels and the ignored folders line are gone
the sideload switch check reads its state file once per call, and not at all while the file is unchanged, instead of three times, which took the event loop about 9 opens a second

the swarm chat composer takes pasted images, dropped files and an attach key: each uploads through the terminal's own upload route into the agent's session folder, shows as a chip, and the send appends the saved paths one per line
two agents or computers sharing a display name no longer crash the home grid: a chart's repeated series names get a short (2) suffix and its legend is keyed by series id

typing into a session on a remote host no longer probes a tmux server of the same name on this mac first, and a remote session's folder is read off its own pane on tmux 3.8 instead of falling back to the far home folder
unstick hands a task's wake-ups to the session that takes it over
update the send-choice connection-count tests to the read-scope lend: a cold call opens one read connection, a warm one none, and a write inside a scope still gets its own
A Codex account with no stored login is no longer looked up in the keychain every poll (shared miss cache with backoff, also used for Claude), and a repeated keychain failure is logged once
A window fully covered by another is now treated like a hidden one: its terminals pause and repaint when it is uncovered
Animations calm automatically while the Mac is in Low Power Mode or running hot

CPU trim: perf_profile counts uvloop async spawns, migration backups keep the newest 2, a Claude profile with no token is not re-read from the keychain every poll, idle agent-type sweeps log at debug, and two routes got their peer forward-table rows
CPU trim: the session listing is rebuilt when tmux says a session or window changed (its own %sessions-changed notice, debounced) instead of every 5 seconds, with a 60 second backstop resync

changes.details: Every infinite animation pauses in place and resumes where it left off; terminals keep streaming. The operating system's Reduce Motion setting now also silences the few pulses that ignored it.
changes.summary: Decorative animations now hold still while the window is unfocused or the Mac is in Low Power Mode or running hot.
Dev perf hook reports the desktop shell's Electron processes and WindowServer CPU/memory
Dev perf hook: with CARNIVORE_DEV_PERF_HOOKS=1 the desktop shell logs app.getAppMetrics() every 10 s to logs/dev-perf.log

changes.details: client/popout.html and client/style-guide.html gain animation-pause.css, motion-setting.js, visibility-observer.js and animation-pauser.js (and the calm script on the guide); test_pauser_reachable_from_every_page.py guards every client page.
changes.summary: Every page that can run an infinite animation now loads the pause machinery (pop-out windows and the style guide were missing it)
Infinite-animation ratchet: a file may not gain an infinite CSS animation (baseline 61 across 24 files)

Listing push follow-up: a tmux change notice now also drops the 1 second owner-listing cache so a new or renamed session shows on the wake pass; subagent, timer, skill, parked-work, MCP, sleep-hold and update marks wake a pass when they move; remote-host sessions keep the 5 second backstop
Listing push: the watcher's listing-mark stamp holds only fields that reach the listing wire, so a subagent's last-activity time no longer wakes the listing pass on every subagent action

changes.details: Card A5 follow-up: resting-row-lights.css stops the three keep-awake steam wisps on any row that is not selected, hovered or focused, at 0.6 opacity. One-file revert.
changes.summary: Non-selected sidebar rows hold their keep-awake steam wisps still

changes.details: Card A5, Carnivore round 2: resting-row-lights.css sets animation none on the breathing ring and working spinner of any row that is not selected, hovered or focused. One-file revert.
changes.summary: Non-selected sidebar rows hold their status lights still (colour still shows state)
Renderer window-state CPU sampler for before/after measurements
Swarm character clock no longer slides its wake-ups later when re-armed mid-sleep, and pausing ends a blink or hop in flight so eyes never stay shut while the window is calm
Swarm character clock wakes on a 250 ms grid by deadline instead of a 100 ms interval, and stops under window calm and OS Reduce Motion

changes.details: The always-mounted filter card re-resolved style every frame behind a hidden card. New test tests/python/design_system/test_popup_focus_steady_wearers.py classifies every popup-focus wearer as transient or on the compositor.
changes.summary: Task manager status filter card stops the popup-focus lap while closed; popup-focus wearer census guard
The desktop app now tells each window when it has been unfocused for a second, so a later change can freeze its decorations
Theme backdrop canvases (matrix rain, sparks and the rest) hold their last frame while the window is calm (blurred, Low Power Mode or thermal pressure) and resume the moment you return.
a JSON web token pasted right after a word character, underscore, digit or hyphen is redacted from its eyJ start again, in messages, redaction and attached files

a card line in a Swarm agent chat (made, dealt, finished and the rest) leads with a card icon; pressing it opens the Swarm board on that card, open in the detail pane and scrolled into view (archived cards on the archived board, a gone card says so)
a close key in the proxy browser's own toolbar, asking first, so the screen can be closed from itself

a computer that joins the pushed list at the instant a change is being sent is no longer sent that change twice (which made it drop and re-subscribe), and the tests now prove each work-off-the-main-loop step on its own and that a cancelled join cleans up

a crate import or Pack migrate gives every imported item its own copy of an attached file, so two items no longer share one file and deleting from one cannot break the other; a file that is not on this computer is dropped with a line in the message saying so (and shown in the Pack migrate summary), and a repair script fixes items imported before

a docx, xlsx or pptx attached to a review board is now read for credentials too, including a key split across runs, in any part, attribute, comment or embedded workbook; one that holds a key is refused, and one that cannot be read (corrupt, encrypted, oversized) is refused instead of passed

a hidden desktop window now holds its terminals and pauses their stream from the app's own hide signal, and resuming a paused terminal can no longer put live output ahead of its repaint or leave it stale after a failed capture
a hidden or minimized app window is now throttled by Electron instead of running at full rate, and goes back to full rate the moment it is shown (reverses R1-10, recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md)

a long message to an agent is no longer pasted two or three times into one prompt: once the paste has run, a slow pane is never re-pasted, Enter alone is retried, and submission is confirmed by reading claude's input box empty

a message sent to a swarm agent that is mid-turn is no longer reported as not submitted: delivery is confirmed from the queued line on screen or the agent's transcript, the text is never pasted twice, and the chat box clears

a one-time reminder set on a back-burner task now takes the task off the back burner and sends the reminder instead of failing with a red clock; a repeating schedule on a back-burner task stays paused

a paired computer's link no longer rewrites its host row and re-announces the roster on every 10 second heartbeat; it does so only when the link state or protocol actually changes, so open windows stop re-fetching the host and peer lists for nothing
a paired computer's old session row is now cleaned up even when a torn-down swarm agent still pointed at it, instead of failing on a foreign key and retrying about 27 times a minute

a paired computer's session list now arrives by push on the events socket it already holds (this Mac's own rows only, nothing owner-only) instead of being re-read every couple of seconds; the old poll stays for a computer that cannot push and while the socket is down

a pink brain at the top right of an agent's chat opens that agent's memory on the right: its index and each fact, readable and editable in the markdown editor; save keeps a backup of the old version first, undo puts the last version back, and earlier versions can be picked and restored

a plugin you sideloaded that asks for a medium or high permission can now be turned on from the Plugins page: its permissions tab shows an untouched tick for each one and a grant button, and your press grants and turns it on in one step
a plugin's inbound webhook refuses a request signed before the app started, so a request captured and used before a restart cannot be replayed after it

a project agent (a company agent for its company's projects) can archive a card at once and ask to delete one, which always waits for your approval even in beast mode; the reason is kept in the card history

a question form's free-text fields (short text, long text and anything else) take a pasted or dropped image: it uploads like a chat paste, shows as a chip with a remove key before submit, and the answer carries the file path to the agent (#2666)

a question one swarm agent asks another now shows in the agent chats as two plain messages, the asker's question and the answering agent's reply, each under its author's name, in the asker's chat and in the chat of the agent it went to; the receipt row with its your message, make craft and kill fact buttons is gone from the chat

a review board attachment holding an Authorization header with a JWT after Bearer is refused again and named as a jwt, not missed or double counted, after the shared secret scan began reporting one finding per credential

a session that joined the swarm keeps its own conversation: its conversation id is recorded again after a fresh start, every automatic wake resumes it, and waking its session from the sidebar marks the agent awake

a settings file whose agent wrappers repeat an id, or leave one out, is refused before the preview, so a second copy can no longer hide a changed command; the command consent shows each wrapper's id and writes hidden or direction-changing characters out instead of drawing them

a settings import no longer drops this install's agent wrappers or changes which one is the default: wrappers merge by id like launch profiles, and an imported wrapper always arrives as not the default; the replace choice now says so, and a replace preview counts the wrappers and launch profiles it keeps

a settings import that would set new or changed environment variables or a new default shell for new terminals now lists each one under contains commands and is refused until each is ticked and the preview's digest is confirmed

a settings import that would set the editor command, the browser program, an account's agent config folder, new quick slash commands or the template folder now lists each under contains commands and waits for its own tick and digest, like the shell and environment

a settings import that would write new or changed agent wrapper commands (script, entry, args, env) now lists them in the preview, says the import contains commands, and is refused until the preview's digest is confirmed, as launch profiles already were; the settings page shows those commands under contains commands, each ticked by hand before apply, which also makes a launch profile import from the page work again
a skill or plugin that ships a plain script file (a .py or .sh at any mode, or any file starting with #!) now asks for code consent at install and update, and never updates on its own

a swarm agent finishing checked, complete work sends its card straight to done; review only holds cards waiting on your answer, pick or hands, with what is needed shown first, and a project agent can close its project's review cards with a reason kept in the card history

a swarm agent's node spikes only when a card asks you for something (a question, a decision, a dialog it is stuck on): a refused or failed wake, a report or a note no longer makes it spiky, and a refused wake card closes once that agent is awake

a terminal the window is not showing (hidden tab or hidden window) tells the server to stop sending its output, and the server sends the current screen once when it is shown again, instead of streaming bytes nobody sees

a wedged tmux server can no longer park the engine's shared thread pool: async control-mode reads wait at most a quarter second and never start the client inline, shutdown no longer blocks on a stuck read client, and a server with only hidden sessions is rechecked once a minute instead of every five seconds
an MCP client that hangs up while sending a request is logged at debug and answered quietly instead of an Exception in ASGI application error with a traceback

an agent can ask several typed questions at once: they reach you as one compact form on its question card in the swarm chat, each row showing only your own answer and a paperclip when you attach a file, the recommended option marked with a yellow star, accept rec filling only the questions you left open, and one send that gives the agent every answer plus the full path of each attached file

an agent's chat box grows upward as you type, up to ten lines or 40% of the chat, then scrolls; attach is a paperclip above send; while you wait on the agent's reply its own character sits under the conversation with a thinking bubble instead of the held line, and goes when the reply posts

an agent's chat no longer scrolls under you while you read older messages: it follows new ones only when you sit at the bottom, and a small down arrow with a count of new messages takes you back to the latest
an agent's empty chat box shows the gray next-prompt suggestion its terminal shows after a turn; Tab fills it in, typing anything hides it, and it is never sent by itself

an agent's node, its question tell and the chat's "waiting on me" now show only what waits on you now: a question no live asker still waits on and a failed-wake card about a torn-down agent stop counting and are closed with a record, a card in Review never counts, and the agent chat drawer starts below the desktop app's title strip so its tabs, filter, menu and close key take a click anywhere on them

an automatic update of a skill that adds code with no execute bit (a hooks file, a settings.json, a shell line in a markdown file) no longer applies silently; it waits for the same consent a manual update asks for, while a text-only update still applies on its own

any command-line coding agent can be a launch profile: type a name and a command and pick an icon, or start from a preset with its logo (pi, oh-my-pi, github copilot cli, devin, factory droid, kimi cli, opencode, kilo code, qoder cli, qwen code, letta, cursor cli, mastra code, antigravity cli, grok cli); its sessions show that name and icon, with no status light

any session can join the swarm as an agent under its project agent, or leave it again, keeping its conversation: a restart warning first, the project agent created on request, cards inventoried on join, cards back to the queue and the agent parked on leave (server, routes and the swarm_join and swarm_leave tools)
clicking the sidebar row of the session that is already open now marks it read, clearing its unread light the way switching to it does, without re-opening or reconnecting the terminal

deleting a task for good now removes its pasted files and attachments from the Task Manager folder, and a task row and an agent chat bar draw no menu button of their own: move to, park, schedule, fork and title are in the row's right-click menu
dialog look: the ring turns on the compositor, every title strip is one shared class, four controls use the one focus rule

do not disturb is gone from the session row menu and the sidebar icon: a swarm member gets leave the swarm in its place and any other session join the swarm; mute means only no notifications from that session, now including the swarm's own pushes and texts from a muted agent
each MCP stdio bridge process uses about 3.8 MB less memory (measured): it no longer loads Python's http.client, email, dataclasses or typing modules, and a test pins that import set
each notes widget shows and saves the note of the session it follows, so two notes widgets on one grid no longer share one note; a widget with no session chosen still follows the selected session

every tmux control-mode read except the reader's own start-up thread is now bounded (about a quarter second, no inline client start), so sync callers on pool threads such as the sessions listing fall back to the subprocess quickly on a wedged tmux server; a client closed under an in-flight read no longer raises
every version bump now runs a public-release export with strict live-state leak gates, and a bump commit is refused without a green report for its tree
give it until on the stuck-wait question is a date and time picker, and i'll handle it parks the task in todo for you

groups can be dynamic: a group's menu has a rule with one icon per attribute (running, sleeping, coffee, sharing, pinned, another computer, swarm, unread, waiting) plus a name prefix and suffix, and every agent matching all of them joins the group live; agents added by hand stay

changes.details: Nine more carnivore.db reads (the stats feed's paired computers, the session records and recent lists, the owned instances, the cplug session ids, the computers page rows, the default master, the relay setting and the waiting-spawn count) now re-read only after a commit and reload on a connection kept per thread instead of opening a new one. The Pack machine block and the provider accounts list are parsed from config.json once per change of the file (its size, time and inode). Issue 1180, slice 6b.
changes.summary: hot database and config reads no longer open the file on every call, even while the database is being written

in a swarm agent's chat, a message from another agent shows that agent's node and no arrow, and a message the agent sent shows the agent's own node with the recipient's tiny node and name at the top of the message, so it is clear who said what and to whom

joining a running session to the swarm no longer fails with "the new body is not on the agent's own session row" when a browser tab open on it reconnects during the restart, and a join that still fails is undone: the agent is parked and the session comes back as a plain session

launch profiles of agents that are not installed on this Mac are hidden from the list and the pickers (never deleted, a show hidden switch brings them back), the new-profile screen has folded examples and one-line hints on agent type, model and permissions, and first run offers an example profile for each installed agent
loopback binds no longer negotiate websocket permessage-deflate (tunnel and relay clients reach the engine on 127.0.0.1 and lose compression on that hop only; the edge compresses its own leg)

mcp health no longer raises the yellow ! on every Claude session for Claude Code's own claude-artifacts built-in: a server that is not in your MCP config and answers HTTP 404 or 501 now reads unknown and stays quiet, while your own servers and every other failure still warn

on a Mac without the developer tools, plugin actions that use git (huddle wait checks, widget lab drafts, crate project snapshots, the plugin runtime's git reads) now go through the same git guard as the rest of the app and degrade quietly instead of raising Apple's install dialog

one filesystem event index over the claude and codex transcript folders now answers codex rollout lookups from a map instead of walking the whole tree, and wakes the attention watcher on a transcript append without re-opening a watch on every pass; a 60 s rescan covers dropped events

opening an agent's chat (a swarm node, a ledger row, a chat name, a huddle row) slides the chat out and keeps the view you were on, narrower beside it, instead of switching to the agent's terminal; the terminal opens only from the chat's own control
pin and unpin in a session row's right-click menu, in the sidebar and on a terminal tab, now actually pin and unpin the session

pushed answers can no longer freeze the token feed or the Pack roster: keepalive frames carry no body so the browser always re-reads and renews its lease, a silent feed re-reads on its own, bodies with NaN are dropped, nothing is built while no owner browser is connected, and one slow build runs at a time

removing a review board attachment deletes its bytes under the same lock that checks no message names them, and a reply that tries to link a just-deleted file is refused, so a thread never links a file that 404s

removing an attachment from a review board now deletes its file from the Task Manager store and replaces its link in the task thread with a removed line, unless another message on the task still carries the same file
reopening a closed task puts it back in the state it had before it was closed (review if none is recorded)
resizing the window while a theme backdrop is held (hidden tab, backdrop switched off, or a calm window) no longer leaves the backdrop blank: one frame is repainted and no animation loop starts

right-click a session (drawer row or sessions page, shift+f10 too) to join the swarm or leave it, after a restart warning (and, when its project has no project agent, a plain statement that ok creates one); a swarm member's row shows its animated swarm character in place of the status light, its animation carrying every status, unread and the startup gate; the projects page row menu toggles new sessions join the swarm
rollback and deploy find the universal release DMG for 1.16.4 and later, and still find the arm64 DMG for older releases, through one shared name helper

server notices such as cannot wake yet and wake failed, with their status changed and approved lines, no longer show as info blocks in any swarm agent chat; the card text in agent chats setting (off by default) now covers them too
server shutdown now runs every teardown step even when an earlier one fails, logging each failure once, and keeps the few steps that depend on an earlier one gated
stale mutation check scripts are retired where an existing test covers the behavior and re-pointed at the moved code otherwise, and a layout fallback test kills the one mutant that survived

starting a new agent now shows a name field and a start pinned box under the agent chooser, prefilled from where the launch started: a project gives its name, a session gives its name with the next free number and its pinned state, a task gives a short form of its title; both can be edited, and an empty name means the default

swarm agents stop saving every message to long-term memory: a fact is a rule or a note, a note expires 14 days after its last use and becomes a rule once 3 separate conversations use it, the chat shows a learned line only for a new rule, project agents prune their own and their children's facts every week and report kept and deleted, and a one-time cleanup can wake every project agent to prune now
test servers and dev-worktree servers now shut themselves down about five minutes after the session that started them is gone, instead of running for days
the MCP stdio bridge answers a request it cannot send (a line break in the pane token or session id) with a clear error and keeps its stream and heartbeat running, instead of killing those threads

the Pack machines list is re-fetched when a machine's membership, state, reserve, restrictions or offers change, and refreshes live load figures every 30 seconds at most, instead of re-fetching every 5 seconds because a CPU reading wobbled

the Swarm roster answers from a one-second cached bare session listing (no listing decorators), dropped by a change notice on every swarm wake, sleep and death, instead of a full listing pass on every poll
the Task Manager add box no longer shows a stray button; Enter in the box files the task straight from the input

the Task Manager plugin's Swarm member face and the reveal wish go through new sdk seams (session.member_face, with a fallback to the plain status light when the plugin is off, and revealWish), and the rail tests register the plugin's own swarm slide-out

the Task Manager's orphan sweep now also cleans each task folder's pastes and artifacts: a stored file no message names is removed after a day, a set-aside copy of a removed attachment after two minutes, and nothing a thread still names, no symlink and none of the owner's other files is ever touched
the add box now keeps a task queued when a session is picked (the pick rides along and the held send goes to it), Enter always submits, and a slow tell can no longer leave the box dead

the agent chat's menu is now the app's one menu, the same panel and hotkey letters as the session row menu: it opens from the kebab, a right click on the chat's title strip or Shift+F10, with the same rows as before; turn off asks in a fold-out and rename asks in the usual text prompt
