the agents drawer's click ladder moves from client/js into typed web/src/lib/drawer modules with the same behavior; the Floor, the sessions search and the mini rail import it instead of reading window.SessionSidebarClicks; the legacy pointer-drag file is retired because the Svelte shell's row drag is the only one that ever ran, and its gesture rules are now pinned by vitest; the inline rename editor moves into web/src/lib/drawer/rename.ts with the same DOM and behavior; the group picker (a row menu's move to a group, and the g key) becomes an item of the one item menu instead of a menu of its own, with the same choices, labels and order, and the legacy group and heading action scripts are retired into typed modules; the row controls script (pin toggle and escapers) and the row menu run table (what each row menu item does, 906 lines) move into typed modules under web/src/lib/drawer and web/src/lib/item-menu/run with the same behavior, and the window.SessionSidebarClicks name is no longer published; a saved Layout row is drawn by a Svelte component through the same row chip component as a session row (same markup and behavior), and the unused group menu styles are removed

the agents drawer's group color, group icon and saved Layouts modules move from client/js into typed web/src/lib/drawer modules with the same behavior and the same window names; a test now pins that docking the drawer refits the terminal

the agents drawer's legacy row reorder script (a facade over the Svelte shell's row keys, focus and drag) is retired; the drawer paint, the search box, the pin menu items and the fetch poll import the shell modules directly, with the same keys, focus, announcements and behavior, and the keyboard cases it carried are pinned by vitest against the shell

the app now trusts first-party carnivore and external releases signed by a cloud KMS key that the pinned root key delegated (custody kms); every other delegation for a first-party handle is still refused
the app pins a spare index key and a spare root publisher key; a statement signed by the spare publisher key moves an install to a replacement root key without an app release

changes.details: The attachable session listing asked tmux twice per pass, once for the sessions (list-sessions) and once for the panes (list-panes -a) whenever the one-second pane cache had expired. Both commands now go to tmux in one process, and the output is split by a tag on each row. The session half is the same list-sessions answer parsed by the same code, so presence and absence are unchanged; a failed or partial read stays unknown. Issue 1180, slice 7c.
changes.summary: the attachable session listing reads tmux in one process per pass instead of two

the attention watcher and the usage-limit auto-restart pass now share one pane-screen cache and one capture function, so a pane read by one is not captured again by the other while tmux shows it has not changed

the background process-table read no longer shows stale command lines for a long-running process that re-executes itself, the pack load figures no longer swing when two readers poll close together, and each read costs less CPU again
the catalog copy and the docs say task manager where they still said huddle (the settings text for the mcp server and the top bell help); no stored name, key, route or tool name changed
the claude session registry reader is split into a record module and an index module with no change in behavior, and every import and patch target follows

the closed drawer now shows the same icon rail as the open one instead of a different set, and the rail's bottom block (account, version, C / 5h / 7d meters) shows in both states; the pin place on the closed rail reopens the drawer

the computers, Pack machines and token feed answers now ride the resources.changed frame itself, built once and sent to every browser, so open tabs apply it with no request and re-read only when the frame has no body (an older server, a phone link, a lease renewal)

the discussion tab's show read button is back on a task whose thread arrived slim: it counts the older messages the server left out and a click reads the whole thread before showing it, and a whole-thread read that was turned away by a write in flight is now asked for again once the write settles

the filesystem event index now keeps claude transcripts and codex rollouts apart, watches transcript roots that appear after start-up, never loses an entry an event added during a rescan, refreshes size and mtime on every rescan, logs what it watches at startup, and the codex presence check no longer lists the sessions folder on every pass
the hosted catalog portal admin takes more than one passkey admin: an ADMIN_EMAILS allow-list, one passkey row and one enrolment window per admin, and a per admin cutover precheck
the intersection-observer scanner test proves it can go red on a tmp_path copy instead of planting a file in client/js, and a static check keeps design_system tests from writing into the repo tree

the launch profile editor no longer offers to pin an account (a pinned profile could never launch), the server refuses to save one with a clear reason, and a profile already saved with a pin still opens and tells you saving it clears the pin
the left icon rail shows every icon by default; edit icons in its menu hides, shows and reorders them, saved for every device

the libproc process snapshot no longer keeps a pre-exec command line after a process execs, reads start times for other users' processes the way ps does, answers ps when libproc returns an empty table, and the pack load CPU reading no longer shortens its own measuring window

the listing push no longer holds the server's event loop while it builds a pass: per-row sleep checks, record projection, JSON serialisation and the diff run on worker threads, so MCP pings and other requests stop queueing behind it

the live lineage scan keeps its place per transcript file instead of per conversation id, so the same conversation in two folders is no longer re-read from the top on every pass; old cursor entries are adopted, not dropped

the one sentence brief on a skill card is written by a model only after you route that feature to a model in settings; a chat default alone no longer turns it on, so no skill text is sent to a model until you choose

the owner, or the agent that attached a file, can delete one file from a task: the thread says it was removed and its bytes are unlinked unless another task names them (DELETE items/{id}/files/{file_id}, task_manager_file_remove)

the pane and session listing is read through one persistent tmux control-mode client instead of starting a tmux process for every read; a down client falls back to the old path, and names are quoted so a crafted session name cannot add a second tmux command

the pane screen read behind the attention watcher and auto-restart goes through the persistent tmux control-mode client, returning the same bytes without starting a tmux process; a down client falls back to the subprocess read

the process table is read from macOS libproc in-process instead of spawning ps -A -ww on every attention, journal and agent-infer pass, ps -ax on every pack load pass and ps -p on every pid-record identity check; a command line is read once per process and kept, so a pass costs a few milliseconds instead of about 76 ms of ps CPU

the pushed computer list is now safe on big or mixed-version setups: an older poll can no longer overwrite a newer push, an oversized list falls back to the poll instead of dropping the events socket, a full copy is re-sent every minute, and only a computer that asks for the push is sent it

the question about a task stuck waiting now says what it waited on and since when, and offers i'll handle it, drop it, check it now and give it until a time you pick; an agent that tries to wait for a known time is told to schedule the task instead

the remaining tmux reads (display-message, show-options, list-sessions, pipe ownership, body death, the pack pane scan and the auto-restart quiet check) go through the persistent control-mode client, so an idle server starts no tmux process for them; a missing target is detected and falls back to the old path

changes.details: ctx.sessions for an outside plugin is no longer a Sessions subclass: it holds a private Sessions and exposes only list, get and the granted message, deliver, booted, asleep and wake. A method added to Sessions later cannot leak to it, and list and get now write one activity row each instead of two or three. Issue 2554.
changes.summary: the restricted sessions capability is a composition-based allow-list instead of inheriting Sessions
the secret scan now detects a five-part encrypted JWT (JWE), bare and after Bearer, in messages, redaction and attached files; one shared pattern replaces the file scanner's own copy

the server log no longer writes one line per routine poll or MCP ping: successful reads and pings are counted into one http_request_rollup line every 5 minutes (count, total, average and max milliseconds per route), while errors, slow requests, writes and sign-in requests keep their own line

the server no longer burns most of a CPU core: the crosstalk expiry timer arms only from messages it can actually expire, so one swarm message held past its deadline can no longer make it re-fire in a tight loop

changes.details: Pooled connections were kept only in a thread-local and never closed when their thread exited; a sqlite3 connection that ran a statement sits in a reference cycle, so its file descriptors stayed open until a cyclic GC pass (rare, because of the GC tuning), and AnyIO workers exit after 10 s idle. ThreadConnections now closes a thread's connections when the thread exits. Every carnivore.db helper also shares ONE per-thread connection (datastore_pool.py) instead of one pool per helper plus a fresh connect per call; a borrow rolls back a transaction a caller left open. The datastore runs PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL under WAL. Issue 2645.
changes.summary: the server no longer strands open database handles when worker threads exit, and shares one database connection per thread instead of opening a new one per lookup
the server's startup and shutdown run as named boot steps in src/core/boot/ instead of one 1,300-line function; same order, same outcomes, same log events
the session listing and the asleep listing are cached for one second and a paired computer reads both in one request, so a paired Mac following this one costs the server far less CPU

the sessions page light, the row menu and the join or leave the swarm action read the swarm roster through an sdk seam the Task Manager plugin registers, and the task clock type moves into the sdk, so removing that plugin no longer breaks them; nothing changes for the user

changes.details: Review fixes for the shared carnivore.db pool. A failed hot read (or a failed schema probe) no longer closes the thread's connection under an outer loan: forget now defers until the last loan ends and only fires on a broken connection, not a busy lock or missing table. Loans are tracked as live tokens, so a dropped token cannot pin later borrows, and the callers that relied on the old no-op close (asleep list, stored records, live ports, name reads, lazy datastore) now release explicitly. kept_read keeps per-opener reuse for openers that own their connection, lineage reads are query_only again, and PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL is reverted so peer grants, revocations and approvals keep full durability. A ThreadConnections pool dropped on another thread hands its connections to the owning thread to close. Issue 2645.
changes.summary: the shared database connection pool no longer closes a connection that a caller is still using, and peer approvals keep full write durability
the sidebar no longer hides and shows again behind the new agent picker when the pointer rests where the rail is
the skills command center no longer lists a Codex home under the accounts folder as a Claude profile group, and the add-on seed no longer reads a Codex home's skills as Claude's

the swarm chat shows the agent's name only, like everywhere else; resting on the name or on its square shows company / project / name, and a click on the name or either square opens that agent's terminal in the middle of the page, the war room's own pop-up (an asleep agent opens its chat); an old message whose author has no live square draws that agent's character resting, never the hollow dashed outline.

the test suite no longer needs a config.json: an autouse fixture points settings at a temp copy of config.example.json, so the boot smoke test and the restart and backend tests pass on a fresh checkout and never read the operator's own file
the text cursor blinks only in the focused terminal, and holds steady while the window is calm or macOS Reduce Motion is on
the themes page build your own guide now names the Carnivore Menubar themes folder and the CARNIVORE_USER_THEMES_DIR override, and its sample theme.json wraps instead of looking clipped

the tmux control-mode read client now answers the folded session+pane listing, the throttle pane scan, pane facts and pane account reads without a spawn; it runs UTF-8 whatever the locale, rejects pane-forged reply guards through a nonce probe, removes its hidden session on shutdown, and never blocks the event loop on a wedged server

the top-down gate no longer refuses a master rebuild because the machine was busy: vitest runs with no per-test timeout, a hung runner is stopped at a 900 s deadline (its whole process group, TERM then KILL) and answers could-not-run with the files still running named, and a test the gate runs may not carry a timeout of its own

the usage-limit auto-restart pass no longer runs a tmux screen capture on every claude pane every 15 seconds: an idle pane whose output has not moved is not read again, and the read right before a restart is still taken fresh

three scheduler tests (a hung wait check, an item_state wait, the nudge sweep) wait on signals the scheduler sends instead of wall-clock budgets, so they no longer fail at random when the machine is loaded

two Task Manager changes made at the same moment (two edits of one item, two moves into one list, a post against a delete, a double answered mark, run now against a tick) can no longer both act on a stale read: the second waits its turn and sees what the first saved
two clicks on a schedule offer at the same moment can no longer both accept it from a stale read: the second waits its turn and is told the offer was already accepted
Automations feed stylesheet keeps comments on their own lines for the public-export structural gate
